[The student asked about] the matter that transcends the Dharmakāya. The Master said, "It is not a withered stump. [The student] asked, "Is it permissible for me to speak of the underlying principle? The Master said, "Yes.
[The student] said, "Is a withered stump not a matter concerning the side of the Dharmakāya? The Master said, "Yes.

[The student] said, "Is what is not a withered stump not a matter that transcends the Dharmakāya? The Master said, "Yes. [The student] said, "As for the Dharmakāya itself, does it encompass all things?"
“There is absolutely nothing,” [Fayan] said. The Master replied, “The Dharma-body is all-pervasive; how could it not encompass this?

Nanquan pointed to a pure water jar and asked, “As for this pure water jar, does it also encompass the Dharma-body? The Master said, “Dharma-ācārya, do not seek the Dharma-body within the confines of the jar.
Nanquan then bowed.

The patriarchs and Buddhas have no intention of deceiving people, yet because people cannot penetrate them, the patriarchs and Buddhas become a deception to people; one cannot say that [they do not deceive].
The Buddhas and Patriarchs do not deceive people. If you can penetrate beyond the Buddhas and Patriarchs, then you have transcended them.
If it is thus, only then can you embody the intent of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; only then will you be equal to those of the "upward direction.

If you have not yet penetrated this, but merely study the Buddhas and study the Patriarchs, then for ten thousand kalpas there will be no time of emergence. A monk asked: "How can one avoid being deceived by the Buddhas and Patriarchs?"
The Master said: "As for the Way, one must awaken to it within oneself before it can be attained.
Chantong, the Zen Master of Beiyuan in Yizhou, first visited Jiashan and asked: "There is no dharma before the eyes; the meaning lies before the eyes.
It is not a dharma of the present moment, nor is it something reached by the ears or eyes. Is this not the Master’s own teaching? Jiashan replied: [Yes.]

The Master said, "It is so. Thereupon, the Master overturned the meditation seat and stood with his hands folded. Yunshan rose and struck him once with a staff; the Master then went down. (Fayan said:
"When he overturned the meditation seat, why did he not leave immediately? He had to wait for him to strike him once with a staff—wherein lay the intent? Subsequently, the Master visited Dongshan.)

Shangtang of Mount Shan said, "Severing the way of the host, one does not fall into a second view. A monk stepped forward from the assembly and said, "One must know there is a person who does not join company.
Shangtang said, "That is still a second view. The monk then overturned the meditation seat.
Shangtang asked, "Old friend, what do you make of this? The monk replied, "I will wait until my tongue is worn away before I speak to you, Master. Later—
When Cui was about to enter the Ling Range, Dongshan said, "Be careful; Feiyuan Ridge is steep and you must look well. The Master remained silent for a long time.
Dongshan called out, "Dharma-heir Tong! The Master responded, "Yes? Dongshan asked, "Why do you not go into the ridge? Thereupon, the Master attained realization and never again entered the ridge.
▲ The Monk Lianhe of Jingzhao Prefecture was a man of unknown origins. His life and deeds were quite extraordinary. He had no fixed abode;
having realized the mind under Dongshan, he lived among the common people in Minchuan. He did not maintain monastic requisites nor did he follow the formal codes of discipline.
Throughout both winter and summer, he wore only a single robe. Day after day, he would go along the riverbanks to gather shrimp and clams to fill his belly.
At dusk, he would sleep amidst the paper money offerings at the White Horse Temple on Mount Dong. The local residents called him the "Shrimp Monk.

When Chan Master Jing of Huayan heard of this, wishing to determine whether he was genuine or not, he first hid himself secretly within the paper money. Deep in the night, as the Master returned, Jing—
The other held him fast and asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master immediately replied, "The wine table and dishes before the deity.
The other let go and said, "It is not in vain that we share the same roots."
▲ Master Qianfeng of Yuezhou ascended the hall and said: "The Dharma-body has three kinds of illnesses and two kinds of radiance;
you must penetrate each one thoroughly before you can return home to sit in peace. You must know that there is still a 'further' opening above this.
Yunmen stepped forward and asked, "Why does the person inside the hermitage not know what is happening outside the hermitage? The Master laughed heartily. Yunmen—
[Daowu] said, "This is still a point of doubt for students. The Master said, "What kind of mental activity is yours? Daowen said, "I also wish for the Master to understand me.
The Master said, "You must be like this before you can sit securely. Daowen responded, "Yes, yes. [The Master] ascended the hall.
"If you raise one, you cannot raise two; to let one point pass is to fall into the second.

Yunmen stepped forward from the assembly and said, "Yesterday someone came from Tiantai and went on to Jingshan. The Master said, "The head cook shall not be required for the communal work tomorrow," and then he descended from his seat.
Miaoxi said, "Both sides are airing their family's disgrace; fortunately, there was no bystander.
Yunmen arrived and said, "I request the Master to answer the question. The Master said, "Have you even reached the old monk yet?
Yunmen said, "So it is? So it is? The Master said, "I thought the monkeys were white; it turns out there are also black ones. [Question: "The Bhagavān of the ten directions..."

The monk asked, "The Brahma King spoke of 'the single path to the gate of Nirvana. I do not know where the beginning of that path lies. The Master drew a line with his staff and said, "It is right here.
Later, the monk requested further instruction from Yunmen. Yunmen picked up his fan and said, "The fan leaps and bounds up to the Thirty-three Heavens, striking the nostrils of Śakra.
A blow from a staff to the carp of the Eastern Sea brings down rain like a basin."
"Inclining. Do you understand?
Baofeng Wen said: "When Qianfeng spoke thus, had he even seen it in a dream? If I were an old monk like me, I would not say so.
'The Buddhas of the ten directions share one path to the gate of nirvana. I wonder where that path begins?"
Strike him across the spine with a staff! Then ask him, "Where is the beginning of the path? Wait until he is about to open his mouth, and shout at him fiercely before driving him out.
Furthermore, there was that old, crippled monk from Yunmen who could not distinguish between the black and the white, nor discern the heterodox from the orthodox;
he would just pick up his fan and say all sorts of things. A fellow like this—muddying the waters and mixing the clay—is fit only to be buried in a heap of dung.
"Set it aside! Whether ten or five, what fault is there? A-he-he! Is it joyful or not? Is it sufficient or not?
Now, fortunately, we face green mountains and blue waters. Year after year, every matter has been brought to rest at once;
let body and mind be free from constraint. Everyone, do not be drowsy!"
He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Tiantai. The Master said, "I heard it was said that the Stone Bridge has been broken in two—is this true?
The monk asked, "From where did you, Reverend, receive this news? The Master said, "I took you for a visitor from the peak of Huading;
it turns out you are a man from the village of Pingtian."
Cen Master Fashiguang visited his former residence. The Master asked, "In recent years, there was one koan that we could not resolve together.
How do you handle it now? The monk replied, "Even before I entered the gate, I had already presented it to you, Master.
The Master said, "What about right here? The monk replied, "One must not add a head atop a head."
The Master drew a line and said, "Let this matter rest for now. Why have you trampled upon the Stone Bridge of Tiantai?
The monk was speechless. The Master said, "You empty-headed liar! Get out! Huanji remarked:
"When these two venerable elders examined the monk, one attained the two kinds of light of the Dharma-body, while the other attained the three kinds of illness of the Dharma-body."
If a person can discern this, they may be said to possess the single eye.
▲ When Chan Master Wensui of Qishan in Lishu was traveling west of the Yangtze River with Yantou and Xuefeng, they arrived at a tea shop.
While drinking tea, the Master said, "Those who cannot turn their bodies and pass through the breath shall not drink the tea. Yantou said, "If..."
[Zhaozhou] said, "In that case, I shall certainly not have tea. Feng said, "I am the same.
The Master said, "These two old fellows do not even recognize the head of the matter. The Head asked, "Where has it gone? The Master said, "An old crow in a cloth bag;
though alive, it is as if dead. The Head stepped back and said, "Look, look! The Master said, "Let us set aside Master Huo for a moment; what about Master Cun?"
Feng drew a circle with his hand. The Master said, "I cannot help but ask. Feng laughed heartily and said, "Too far!
The Master said, "There are many who have mouths but cannot drink the tea. The Zen guest Jili came to pay his respects.

Having finished his prostrations, he asked, "What is it like when a single arrowhead pierces the three barriers? The Master said, "Let out the master of the barrier and look. Jili said, "In that case..."
"If that were so, one would surely know to reform one's errors. The Master said, "When do you intend to do so? Yuanliang said, "What a fine arrow—it was released but did not hit its mark!
He then went out. The Master called, "Dharma-teacher, wait a moment! Yuanliang turned his head.

The Master stepped down from his meditation seat, seized him, and said, "Setting aside for a moment the fact that a single shaft pierced the three barriers, try now to discharge an arrow for Qingshan. Yuanliang hesitated. The Master—
Striking him seven times with his staff, he said, "Listen for a moment, you confused fellow! You have harbored doubts for thirty years. A monk reported this to Tong’an Cha.
Tong’an said, "Although Master Liang knows how to release the arrow, he has yet to hit the mark. The monk then asked, "I wonder how one might hit the mark?
Tong’an replied, "Who is the Lord of Guanzhong? The monk returned and reported this to the Master (Zhaozhou). The Master said:
He said: "If Master Liang understands it in this way, he too might avoid the mouth of Master Qin. Nevertheless, although this is so, Tong’an did not have good intentions;
you must examine this further before you can grasp it."
Xuedou Xian’s verse says: "I release for you the Lord of Guanzhong; You who would shoot arrows, do not be reckless! If you take this eye, the ears will surely go deaf;
If you lose this ear, the eyes will be doubly blind. Pitifully, a single shaft breaks through the three passes;
Clearly and distinctly, the path lies behind the arrow. Have you not seen what Xuansha said? 'A great man...'"
"Preceding heaven is the ancestor of the mind. Tian Tong Jue said: "The mountains are pushed forward and the peaks accumulated;
they disintegrate like tiles and melt away like ice. Thus, people of this age know it exists. Let me let out the Lord of Guanzhong for you to see—how should one act?
Some say: "At that moment, he would have shouted; at that moment, he would have struck with his palm. However, such is a blind application for a single occasion.

Yes, you have attained it. But for now, you are not yet the master of the central pass. Have you realized this? If one does not sit upright in the hall itself, how can one respond to the pivotal functions of both extremes?
A monk asked Chan Master Jiufeng Tongxuan of Ruizhou, "Can the self-mind and the other-mind see each other? The Master said:

He said: "If one cannot even see oneself, how can one observe another? On the seventeenth day of the second month in the third year of the Qianning era of the spurious Tang dynasty, he rose at dawn and exhorted his disciples, saying:
"Do not let the light of time pass in vain; do not let the offerings of the faithful go to waste.

Having already left the household life, walk only in the Way; this is what it means to be a great man. Thereupon, he entered a state of silent meditative concentration (*samādhi*). This continued until the third month.
On the twentieth day, he passed away. He had lived in this world for sixty-three years and sat in meditation for forty-two summer retreats.
The Master cited the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* to clarify the five ranks; the details of his discourse are contained within the "Chapter on the Five Ranks of Dongshan."
The Record of Pointing at the Moon, Volume XVIII and Volume XIX:
The Seventh Generation after the Sixth Patriarch.
When Minister Chen Cao came to visit Zen Master Ru Bao of Zifu Temple in Jizhou, the Master drew a circle.
Cao said, "I have come this way, yet I am already at a disadvantage; why do you draw another circle? The Master placed a single dot in the center.
Cao said, "I thought you were the master of a ship from the Southern Barbarians. The Master then returned to his quarters and closed the door.
▲ Master Huìqīng of Bājiāoshān in Yǐngzhōu ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he addressed the assembly, saying:
"If you have a staff, I give you a staff; if you have no staff, I take your staff away.
He leaned on the staff and descended from the seat.
Daguizhe said: "Daguizhe does not do it this way. When you have a staff, I take away your staff;
when you have no staff, I give you a staff. Daguizhe acts thus. Have you all yet been able to employ it?
If one can employ it, Deshan is the vanguard and Linji is the rear guard. If you can employ it..."
"You may not have it; return it to its original owner. Tiantong Zhengjue said: "If you have it, then everything has it.
If you do not have it, then everything lacks it. Having or lacking is simply a matter for the person themselves.
Granting or taking away is but a trivial affair, like a banana tree. At this very moment, what is your staff?"
Question: "When a thief comes, one must strike; when a guest comes, one must welcome. But what if both a guest and a thief arrive at the same time?
The Master said, "In the house there is a pair of worn-out straw sandals. [The monk] asked, "As for those worn-out straw sandals, are they still fit for use?"
The Master said, "If you take this with you, there will be misfortune ahead and no good fortune afterward.
The Master said to the assembly, "When I was twenty-eight years old, I went to Yangshan to visit Nanta. I saw him ascend the hall and say: 'All of you here—if you are a man of true caliber...'"
"Upon emerging from my mother's womb, I uttered a lion’s roar; was it not so? At those words, my body and mind came to rest, and I remained there for five years."
▲ Chan Master Huīyǒng of Nányuàn in Rùozhōu (also known as Bǎoyìng) ascended the hall and said: "Upon the bare flesh-ball, it stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high.
A monk asked, "Is it not you, Master, who said that upon the bare flesh-ball it stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high? The Master replied, "It is."
The monk then overturned the meditation seat. The Master said, "This blind donkey is acting recklessly. As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him and drove him out.
Miaoxi said, "I now guarantee this matter for you; it shall never be in vain. He then added a verse: *Chi* (Red).
At the edge of the lump of flesh, usage is intimate; host and guest have their reasons, yet each finds it difficult to prevail.
When two hunchbacks meet, there are no upright people left in the world today.
He asked the monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Xiangzhou. The Master said, "What have you come for?
The monk said, "I have come specifically to pay my respects to the Master. The Master said, "It happens that Old Baoying is not here.

The monk then shouted. The Master said, "I told you he was not here; why did you shout again? The monk shouted once more. The Master struck him. The monk bowed. The Master said, "This blow was originally..."
"It was you who struck me; let me strike you back. I want this story to spread far and wide. [The Master] said, "Blind fellow, go to the hall!
He asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Xiangzhou. The Master said, "What kind of thing comes here like this? The monk said, "Try saying it yourself, Teacher.
The Master said, "The one who just bowed—that one? The monk said, "Wrong. The Master said, "In what way was the one who bowed wrong?"
[The monk] said, "A second offense will not be tolerated. The Master said, "For thirty years I have been riding horses;
today I am knocked down by a donkey. You blind fellow, go to the hall! A monk asked, "Where have all the sages of the past gone?
The Master said, "Neither to heaven nor into hell. The monk asked, "And what about you, Master? The Master said, "Do you know this old fellow Baoying?"
"Where does it land? The monk hesitated. The Master struck him with a whisk and said, "Do you know who it is that eats the whisk?
He replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The true command is actually being carried out by you," and struck him with the whisk once more.
Xuedou said: "The command has already been executed; furthermore, the whisk does not know its place of origin.
Xuedou uttered the word "blind," which was intended to add frost to the snow. Miaoxi said:
"To weigh Linji’s Three Essentials and Three Mysteries, one must look to Nanquan; why then did Xuedou say that the whisk does not know its place of origin?"
Miaoxi also said, "Blind! He did this merely to ensure that the two could meet.

He asked a monk, "What is your name? The monk replied, "Puchan. The Master said, "If you suddenly encounter a wooden stake, what will you do? The monk said, "I do not know. The Master then struck him.
He ascended the hall and said: "The various quarters [of the Chan schools] possess only the 'eye of simultaneous pecking and hatching,' but they do not possess the 'eye of pecking and hatching.'"
[The Master] used the "simultaneous pecking and hatching. A monk then asked, "What is the simultaneous use of pecking and hatching?

The Master said, "A master does not peck and hatch; at the moment of pecking and hatching, one loses it. The monk said, "This is still not where I was asking. The Master said, "How is it at the place where you were asking?
The monk said, "I have lost it. The Master struck him. That monk did not accept this, and later, while under Yunmen’s assembly, he heard...
Two monks were discussing this story. One monk said, "At that time, did not Nan-yuan’s staff break? Suddenly, the other monk attained awakening.
He then hurried back to pay his respects, but the Master had already passed away. He subsequently went to visit Feng-xue.

As soon as Feng-xue saw him, he asked, "Monk, are you the one who at that time questioned the former Master about the 'simultaneity of the peck and the hatch'? The monk replied, "I am. Feng-xue said, "You..."
"How did you understand it at that time? he asked. Yunmen replied, "At that moment, it was as if I were walking within the shadow of a lamp.
Xuefeng said, "You have understood.
Wuzu Yunju remarked, "But what is this 'eye of simultaneous pecking and hatching'? If one attains clarity of eye, then..."
Use it for yourself; furthermore, the master of the Way does not wait for the "pecking" and "breaking. If pecking and breaking occur simultaneously, one loses [the Way].
Why do they not wait for the pecking and breaking? Therefore it is said: "If the child lets out a roar, the mother immediately perishes. Can you all clearly understand this? He then spoke in verse:
"If the child lets out a roar, the mother immediately perishes; Fully returning to the child, the ten directions are unobstructed. Great!
By means of the principle of what is manifest before one, it is naturally so; why must you stir the mind to create a semblance? Furthermore, if you do not understand, consider Yunju’s staff:
as soon as a monk entered the abbot’s quarters to inquire, Yunju pointed with his finger and said, "Defeated! The Master then picked up his staff and passed it to him.
The monk had barely reached out when the Master struck him.
Yunfeng Yue said, "Although this monk has a radiance upon his head, he does not realize that beneath his feet he is as dark as lacquer.
Even if one were to strike three thousand times in the morning and eight hundred times in the evening, regardless of how the ten directions are traversed."
▲ Attendant Shoukuo asked Deshan, "Where have all the sages of antiquity gone? Deshan said, "What? What?
The Master [Shoukuo] said, "The imperial decree summons the flying dragon horse; yet a lame turtle pokes its head out. Deshan then ceased speaking.
The next day, as the Master was emerging from his bath, Master Shanshan passed by him with tea. Shanshan patted him on the back once and said, "What about yesterday’s *kōan*?
The Master replied, "This old fellow; it is only today that you have finally woken up. Shanshan then let the matter rest.

Later, while traveling on pilgrimage, the Master arrived at the assembly of National Teacher Huayan in Xiangzhou. One day, Huayan ascended the hall and addressed the assembly, saying: "Great assembly!"
"If you today are the descendants of Linji, Deshan, Gaoteng, Dayu, Niaoke, and Chuanzzi, there is no need for 'how' or 'what.
I request that you enter directly with a single blade; Huayan shall provide you with verification. The Master came forward and prostrated.

As soon as he rose, [Fengxue] gave a shout. Yanyou also shouted. The Master shouted again; Yanyou shouted once more. The Master rose from his prostrations and said, "The assembly, look at this old fellow’s total defeat!
He then gave another shout, clapped his hands, and returned to the assembly. Yanyou descended from the seat and went to the abbot’s quarters.
At that time, Fengxue was serving as the *karmadāna* (Venerable of the Hall). As he went up to offer his greetings, Yanyou said, "Karmadāna, you have come. How vexing!"
"Shoukuo just now came and gave this old monk a good twisting and squeezing. I was waiting to assemble the assembly to give him a beating and drive him out.
Xue said, "It is too late to drive him out; it was simply the Master’s own words that were excessive. He is a descendant of Linji; such is his natural disposition.
Yan Fang then calmed his anger. Xue went down and reported this to the Master. The Master said, "For what reason did you do this?"
[The Master] exhorted this fellow: "Before I had even asked you, you already wanted to eat my staff so that my words might be put into practice.
If I do not strike you now, you will surely obstruct these words of mine. Xue said, "Even so, they have already spread throughout the world.
When the Master arrived at Lumen, one day he saw Monk Chu engaged in conversation with a monk. As Lumen came down [from his quarters], he asked Monk Chu:
"What are you doing all day long, wearing your robes so loosely? Chushi said, "Does the Master see me wearing my robes loosely?
Baizhang gave a shout; Chushi also shouted. Both men then ceased their activity. The Master said, "Venerable ones, look at these two blind men!
He then followed them with a shout. Baizhang returned to his quarters and ordered an attendant to invite the Master up.
Linji said, "The old monk just now had an encounter with Chan-jre as guest and host.
Where was there a failure? Dongshan said, "I see your illness is becoming even deeper. Linji said, "Since I first met Xinghua, I have understood.
Dongshan said, "When you were at Xinghua, I was your attendant; do you remember what was said at that time? Linji said, "Please cite it for me. Dongshan said, "Please cite it."
"Look! The Master then related: "Xinghua asked a monk, 'Where have you come from? The monk replied, 'From Wutai.
Xinghua asked, 'Have you seen Mañjuśrī? The monk gave a shout. Xinghua said, 'I asked you if you had seen Mañjuśrī;
why do you act so aggressively? The monk shouted again. Xinghua remained silent. The monk bowed. The next day, Xinghua instructed [the assembly]:"
"Such-and-such a person is calling for the Master. "The Master has already departed. Hua went up to the hall and said, "Look at this monk!
Carrying a broken rope, he is heading south. Later on, he will also say that he has seen Xinghua.
The Master said, "Today’s case is exactly like that from those times. Mun asked, "Why was it that Xinghua remained silent at that moment? The Master said, [as before].

He said, "I saw that the Master did not understand the phrase regarding host and guest, which is why I did not speak. When I wished to call upon the Master to engage in debate, the Master had already departed.
On the following day, Lumen specifically prepared tea for the assembly. At the evening *can*, he addressed the congregation, saying:

"Those who study as dragons and elephants must enter the room with thorough discernment and make a definitive choice; they must not take it lightly, thinking they have grasped some mere phrase and then [stop]."
He took this to be the ultimate; he considered himself spiritually sharp. It was just as when I first met Xinghua:
I recognized his shifting movements, and when people spoke of "one shout" or "two shouts," I simply stopped there and took that to be the Buddha-dharma.
Today, having been seen through by those with clear eyes, it has become nothing but a source of ridicule. What was the point? It was solely because of my own arrogance.
Ignorance prevents one from turning back to draw near to those who flow upward;
it is only by relying on a man of the Way with clear eyes that one can, without sparing body or life, provide testimony before the assembly. This kindness is difficult to repay. Why? Xinghua said:
"Even if you were to shout yourself up to the thirty-third heaven and then crash back down until you had not a breath left, you would still have to slowly recover."
"Get up! I have not yet finished speaking to you. Why do you act like this? Xinghua has never scattered real pearls from within a purple silk curtain for you;
why do you shout and roar so recklessly? These are truly words of medicinal admonition, yet it is difficult for practitioners (dàoliú) to believe them.
Now you must discern them clearly; will this not bring joy to your entire life and bring an end to your studies?"
▲ When the Venerable Shi from West Yuan in Ruzhou arrived at the Dharma seat, he remained for ten days.

He often said to himself, "Let alone those who claim to understand the Buddha-dharma; there is not even a single person to be found who can raise a koan. Upon hearing this, the Master remained silent.
On another day, as Yi was ascending to the Dharma Hall, the Master called out to him by name. Yi raised his head, and the Master said, "Wrong.

Yi took two or three steps forward, and the Master said again, "Wrong. Yi approached even closer, and the Master said, "Those two previous 'wrongs'—was it the Senior Monk’s fault, or was it the old fellow Siming’s fault?
Yi replied, "It was Yi’s fault. The Master said, "Wrong, wrong! He then said, "Senior Monk, stay right here for a moment."
"I spent the summer retreat here to deliberate with you on these two errors. Yì was unwilling to leave immediately. Later, he resided at Mount Tiānpíng in Xiāngzhōu.
Every time he brought up the previous story, he would say: "When I was traveling on pilgrimage, I was blown by an evil wind to Rǔzhōu.
There was an elder, the West Hall Abbot, who examined me regarding those two successive errors and further requested that I stay for the summer retreat so that we might deliberate together."
"I do not say it was wrong at that time. When I first set out for the South, I already knew it was wrong.
Shoushan Nian said, "According to Tianping’s way of understanding this, he has not even dreamed of Xiyuan yet. Why?
Because the matter lies in the words. Yuanwu Keqin said, "Nowadays, when people hear him say, 'When I first set out for the South...'"
One should have known it was wrong from the very beginning when departing. Yet one immediately engages in speculative calculation, thinking:
"Before I set out on pilgrimage, I naturally possessed none of this abundance of Buddha-dharma, Chan, or the Way. But once I went on pilgrimage, I was thoroughly deceived by those everywhere.
This is not to say that before setting out on pilgrimage, you were calling earth heaven or mountains water; fortunately, there was not a single speck of such business. If it were all like that...
To hold such worldly views—why not simply buy a hat and wear it? When everyone is merely passing through this world, what use is there for that?
The Dharma is not a matter of such principles.

▲ When Master Baoshou (the Second Generation) was serving as the *kōmyōshu* (offering master) at the former Baoshou Temple, Baoshou asked him, "Before your parents were born, bring me back your original face.
The Master stood there until late at night, yet his response did not accord with the truth. The following day, he took his leave.
Baoshou said, "Where are you going? The Master replied, "Yesterday I received the Master’s question, but I could not accord with it."
"I am going south to visit a spiritual friend. Shou said, "In the south, the summer retreat is observed but not the winter retreat;
here, we observe the winter retreat but not the summer retreat. You should spend the summer as a street-walker (beggar).

If it is the Buddha-dharma, even amidst the vast red dust of the marketplace, the True Dharma is constantly preached. The Master did not dare to disobey. One day, he saw two people quarreling on the street.
He struck out a single blow and said, "You have attained such facelessness. At that moment, the Master attained great enlightenment.
He went to see Baoshou, but before he could utter a word, Baoshou said, "You understand; there is no need to speak. The Master then prostrated himself.

When Baoshou was about to pass away, he instructed Sansheng to invite the Master to open the hall for formal preaching. On the day the Master opened the hall, Sansheng pushed forward a monk. The Master—
He struck him. The Master said, "To teach people in such a manner will not only blind this monk's eyes, but will also blind the eyes of the entire city of Zhenzhou.
The Master then threw down his staff and returned to his quarters.
Yunfeng Yue said: "The single school of Linji has been swept away and exhausted. For what reason, then, have you arrived here?
He suddenly took up his staff and said, "Where have you gone? Zhenjing’s Verse: A wild horse gallops in, fierce beneath the staff;
Blind men fill the city of Zhinzhou. Peace was originally brought about by the generals, But they are not permitted to remain.

The army beholds Great Peace; this is the Verse on True Suchness (*tathatā*). Who will the Dharma-Eye be entrusted to? The Three Sages deliberate with the monks to resolve the doubts of the multitude.
The General’s command is issued and the common people are struck with awe; it truly causes the sound of the blind to reach the four barbarian frontiers.
As the Master was about to pass into nirvana, he said to his disciples, "Do you know where I have been traveling? They replied, "We know;
for many years, you, O Monk, have sat upright and never lay down. The Master again called a monk to come forward. When the monk had approached, the Master said, "Go;
you are not one of my kin. Having finished speaking, he passed away.
A monk asked Chan Master Changcha of Tong’an Monastery in Fengxi, Hongzhou: “The student does not yet understand the timing;
I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said: “Sparse pines and bamboos enshroud the mist thinly; layered peaks and ridges wait long for the moon to rise.”
The monk prepared to offer a word, but the Master said, "Before the armor and blades are even deployed, the thief’s body has already been exposed. The monk asked, "Why?
The Master said, "A refined bamboo from before the frost need not be trimmed; ink and water vainly boast of the dragon of the sea. The monk circled the meditation seat and departed.
The Master said, "Closing one's eyes to eat a snail—what a bitter and sour experience!

A newly arrived monk circled the Master three times with his staff, struck it once, and said, "Please speak, Master, regarding that place where neither ordinary beings nor sages reach. The Master snapped his fingers three times.
The monk said, "Today, Tongan has frightened me into forgetting what came before and losing track of what follows. The Master asked, "Where did you set out from, *āyuṣmat*? The monk—
"Take care," he said, and then he went out. The Master said, "Monks from the five lakes, practitioners with their single staff: before you have reached Tong'an, you will not fail to harbor doubts.
The monk turned his head and said, "Hearing from afar is not as good as seeing nearby. The Master said, "In greed for a single cup of wine, one loses the fish in the entire boat.
He asked another monk, "Where have you recently come from? "From Jiangxi," he replied. The Master said, "The Dharma-way of Jiangxi..."
"What is it like here? [Nanquan] said, "Fortunately, I have encountered you to ask me this. Had you asked anyone else, disaster would have ensued.
The Master said, "I was somewhat hasty just now. [Nanquan] said, "I am no infant; do not use the yellow leaves that merely stop a child's crying."

The Master said, "I feel pity for the turtle and spare it; whether to kill or to let live depends on me. The monk asked again, "Having long cultivated the profound mystery, how does one attain thorough understanding?
The Master said, "This old monk is hard of hearing; ask clearly. The monk said, "A swift falcon does not strike at the sparrows by the fence."
[The Master] said, "When a master looks into a mirror in the dark, who can distinguish the beautiful from the ugly? [The monk] asked, "How does one thoroughly understand the higher mechanism?

The Master said, "Why bother? [The monk] said, "Enough, enough. The Master said, "Only then do you understand how to board a boat; you still intend to leap across the Sword River. He questioned a monk, "Where have you come from?
The monk replied, "Wutai. The Master said, "Have you seen Mañjuśrī? The monk spread out both hands. The Master said, "Spreading hands."

[The monk] said, “Very many. Mañjuśrī [the painting] was difficult to behold. [The monk] said, “It makes me gasp for breath! The Master said, “If you do not see the wild geese in the clouds, how can you know the cold of the desert sands?
[The monk] said, “I have come from afar to your chamber; I beg the Master for a single word. The Master said, “Under Sun Bin, they merely talk of divining by tortoise shells.
[The monk] said, “A name is not acquired without reason. The Master said, “Go and drink tea. The monk, having paid his respects, departed. The Master said, “Although...”
To gain one moment of glory, one must lose a pair of feet. The Master asked a monk, "When the realm of the eye has no light, how can one see?
The monk replied, "The Big Dipper turns east; the Southern Dipper shifts west. The Master said, "It is like a Confucian entering the Grand Ancestral Temple.

The monk said, "In that case, under the gate of Tong’an, the Way is cut off and the path is desolate. The Master said, "Holding an infant crosswise in one’s arms, intending to manifest the imperial majesty."

One day, while Master Jian was touring the mountains, the assembly followed him. The Master said, "The green bamboos before the steps, the yellow chrysanthemums beneath the terrace—ancient worthies called these 'True Suchness' and 'Prajñā.
Tongan, however, would not have it so. At that time, a monk said, "The ancients were good, but what about the Master?
The Master replied, "Not craving the taste of fragrant bait, he may truly be called a dragon in the azure pool. [The monk] said, "He is the eye of all quarters."

The monk did not find it strange that Tao Qian [closed his eyes]. The Master said, "When you, Dharma brother, sat with your eyes closed on the Mid-Autumn Festival, why did you instead find it strange that the moon had no light?

The monk replied, "What about the green bamboos before the steps and the yellow chrysanthemums at the base of the wall? The Master said, "Annam has not yet submitted; how could the northern frontier have been conquered?
The monk bowed, and the Master said, "His fame is heard everywhere. He then asked another monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Tai..."
Yuan asked, "Master, how is the Way of the Dharma in Taiyuan these days? The Master said, "I see only clouds following the rising sun and water following the ripples;
I do not know how the Way of the Dharma is in Taiyuan. The Master said, "Is it not that you have left Taiyuan? He replied, "Bitter! Bitter!
The Master said, "One does not behold the color of the ocean clouds, yet one faintly perceives the sound of a drought thunder. He replied, "Exchanging gold for brass; I detest this."
"True love is a sham. The Master then returned to his quarters. The monk brushed out his sleeves and departed. The Master said, "When you can tuck in your head, tuck it in.
Next was Wuyin of Heishan in Jizhou. He was born into the Wu family and was a native of Fuzhou. At the age of seven, Xuefeng Congzhen...

When the Chan Master saw him, he admired his purity and sincerity. He converted the youth’s parents and had them allow him to leave the household life. At the age of twenty, he shaved his head and received full ordination.
Taking his leave to travel to various regions, he arrived at Jiufeng. Master Qian asked him, "Having come from afar, what have you seen? By what path should one emerge from birth and death?
He replied, "The deep darkness has been cleared away; the blind remain blind. Master Qian smiled and brushed him away with his hand.
He said, "The Buddha-dharma is not like this. The Master was displeased and asked, "Is there no expedient means? He replied, "Ask me. The Master repeated his previous words and questioned him again.
He said, "A master sees the diligence of a servant. The Master then remained in attendance for over ten years. To inquire and study is called *wen* (hearing);
to cease inquiry and study is called *lin* (neighborhood). To transcend both of these is called *zhen guo* (true transcendence). It is as follows:
"What is the true fault? The Master said, "Heshan knows how to beat the drum. [The monk] asked, "What is the Absolute Truth (*paramārtha*)?
The Master said, "Heshan knows how to beat the drum. He asked, "I do not ask about 'this very mind is Buddha,' but what is 'neither mind nor Buddha'?
The Master said, "Heshan knows how to beat the drum. He asked, "What is the matter that transcends this? The Master said, "Heshan knows how to beat the drum."
Xuedou’s Verse: One drags a stone, two carry earth; To trigger the mechanism, one must have a crossbow of a thousand catties.
The Old Teacher Xianggu once rolled a ball; How does he compare to Heyuan, who knows how to beat the drum?
I inform you: do not be reckless! The sweet is sweet, and the bitter is bitter. In various quarters, this is called "Heyuan’s Four Drum Beatings. Furthermore, a monk asked Master Hu...
Guo Cheng asked, "When a crane stands atop a withered pine, what then? Cheng said, "A scene of utter embarrassment beneath one's heels.
He asked again, "When snow covers the thousand mountains, what then? Cheng said, "After the sun has risen, a scene of utter embarrassment. He asked once more.
During the Huichang persecution of the Buddhist teachings, a Dharma-protecting deity asked, "Where have you gone?
Cheng replied, "Outside the main gate, two fellows are quite embarrassed. The various quarters call this "The Three Embarrassments of Protecting the Nation.
Furthermore, Baofu asked a monk, "What Buddha is in the hall? The monk said, "Wait for the Master to decide. Baofu said, "Śākyamuni Buddha."
The monk said, "It would be better not to deceive people. Fokuang said, "In fact, it is you who are deceiving me. He then asked the monk, "What is your name? The monk replied, "Xianze.
Fokuang said, "What if you encounter a time of drought? The monk said, "Who is it that suffers from drought?"
Fengxue said, "It is I. Baofu said, "Master, you should not deceive people. Fengxue said, "In fact, it is you who are deceiving me.
He then asked another monk, "What karma have you performed that you eat so much? The monk said, "The Master is not small either. Baofu made a squatting gesture.
The monk said, "Master, you should not deceive people. Baofu said, "In fact, it is you who are deceiving me. He asked yet another.
The master of the bathhouse asked, "How wide is the bath cauldron? The Master said, "Please let the Abbot measure it for you. Fubao made a gesture of measuring it.
The master said, "Abbot, you had better not deceive people. Fubao said, "In fact, it is you who are deceiving me.
This is known in all quarters as "Baofu’s Four Deceptions. Song’an Xian cited these three kinds of speech, saying: "Do you all wish to understand? Xian..."
The Elder has versified it for you. The verse says: Heshan beats the drum; Huguo is bashful; Baofu deceives people—these three are like flower-buds.
For your sake, I have versified them all in one word: *Suo* (the lock).
In the second month of the first year of the Jiànlóng era (the Gēngshēn year), he manifested a slight illness.

On the second day of the third month, he instructed his attendant to open the abbot’s quarters and assemble the great assembly, saying: "Those who come here to study later on have not yet recognized Heshan; recognize him right now!
Thereupon, he passed away peacefully.
Hong Juefan said: "Shishuang stated that 'the entire realm has never been hidden,' yet when his disciple Wengu was on the verge of passing away, [Shishuang] said:
'Today I shall speak clearly to you; when I close my eyes, listen all at once. Jiufeng stated that 'the entirety of heaven and earth is your own true self;
where would you place your eyes, ears, nose, and tongue? Yet his disciple Yin..."
As the Master was approaching his passing, he said: "Those who come later and study the Dharma have not yet recognized Heoshan; recognize him this very moment!
I observe that the words and deeds of this father and his sons and brothers are like a form casting a shadow or a sound echoing from a valley;
yet the Chan practitioners of recent times still linger in deliberation—how truly lamentable!
▲ One day, Master Chan Chuanchu of Qingfeng in Fengxiang Prefecture was asked by Luopo: "Where has the head monk been?
The Master replied, "I have been coming from sweeping the snow. Luopo asked, "How deep is the snow? The Master said, "It is all over the trees.
Luopo said, "That is fine, but you will surely dwell in a 'snow cave' in the future. Later, he visited Baihui, who said, "I see..."
[Zhaozhou] said, "Luopu speaks of a path of vital energy (*jīshēng*). Is this so? The Master said, "It is. Zhaozhou said, "Block off the path of life and come from the path of maturity.
The Master said, "On the path of life there are countless dead people; on the path of maturity no living man finds a place."
Shui said, "This is the bottom of Luopu; what about yours? The Master said, "Not only Luopu, even Jiashan could do nothing about it.
Shui asked, "Why could Jiashan do nothing about it? The Master said, "Have you not heard it said:
'The single path of the living mechanism'?"
▲ When Chan Master Shandao of Mount Muping in Yuanzhou first visited Luopo, he asked: "Before a single bubble has yet arisen, how does one discern the flow of the water?
Luopo replied: "Shift the boat and you will know the current; raise the oar and you will distinguish the waves. The Master did not find resonance with this, so he went to study under Panlong.
He asked the same question as before. Panlong said: "If you shift the boat, you do not need to distinguish the water; if you raise the oar, it is already..."
The Source of Delusion. The Master attained awakening from this.
Yunfeng Yue said, "If Muping had awakened upon hearing Luopo’s words, he would still have been slightly better off.
What a pity! He was drowned in the stagnant water of Panlong. Later, someone asked, "What is Muping? [He] replied:

He said, "No need for the axe; indeed, it is right here. All you Zen practitioners, whenever you set out to travel and study, you must distinguish between the heterodox and the orthodox, and discern the genuine from the counterfeit. Only when you possess some measure of the "eye-fiber" can you succeed.
Even so, this is like drawing a bow after the thief has fled. Miaoxi said, "Yunfeng’s words here can also blind people's eyes."
He was also able to open the eyes of others.
▲ Chan Master Tongquan of Yingzhou went to visit Huangshan. Huangshan asked, "When the Gate of Heaven is closed, there is no path in the ten directions.
If someone can speak, they may wave their hand and depart across the Zhang River. The Master said, "The hibernation chamber does not open; the dragon has no dragon-phrase."
Mount [Shan] said, "Is it as you say? The Master said, "If it is so, speak directly that it is; if it is not, speak directly that it is not.

Mount Shan said, "Waving his hand, he departs through the Zhang River. Mount Shan asked again, "When Xiahuo says, 'Everywhere the mountains of Jing are beautiful, the jade seal is passed on by the Son of Heaven,' what then?
The Master said, "The numinous crane does not rest beneath the forest trees; the village elder does not value [the seal]."
The Year of Great Peace. Shanshen approved of this (the Yi says: "One blind man leading many blind men—how tragic!").
Chan Master Shiyuan of Ruiyan in Taizhou was the son of the Xu family in Min. From childhood he donned the black robes [of a monk], and his observance of the precepts was without flaw.
Initially, he paid respects to Yantou, who asked him: "What is the fundamental principle of constancy? Yantou replied: "Movement. [Shiyuan] said: "Movement..."

"How is it at such a time? Tou said, "It is not the fundamental, constant principle. After the Master had remained silent for a long while, Tou said, "If you accept this, you have not yet shed the root and dust;
if you do not accept it, you will sink forever into birth and death. The Master then attained realization and prostrated himself. Later, he went to visit Jia Shan.
Mount Shishuang asked, "Where have you come from? The master replied, "I have come from Wo-long. Shishuang said, "When you came, had the dragon yet risen? The master looked around him.
Shishuang said, "This is like applying moxa to a scar from a previous burn. The master said, "Why do you trouble yourself so much, Master? Shishuang then desisted.
Miaoxi said, "If he had not shot the stone tiger at Lan-tian, he would have nearly killed General Li by mistake.
The Master asked Jia-shan, "In this way it is easy; in another way it is difficult. In this way and that way, one is truly alert."
"Not so, not so" is to dwell within the realm of emptiness. "So, not so"—I beg the Master to speak quickly!
The Master said, "This old monk is deceiving you, Layman. The Master (Xuedou) shouted, "This old monk! What kind of time is this now?
and then he went out.
Later, a monk recounted this to Yantou, who said, "Alas! You are carrying away my branch of the Buddha-dharma in such a manner.
The Master subsequently resided at Ruiyan in Danqiu; sitting upon a flat rock, he remained as if ignorant all day long, constantly calling out to himself, "Master! (Zhongzhugong).
He again assented and said, "Stay alert! Hereafter, do not allow yourself to be deceived by others. Later, a monk visited Xuansha.
Xuansha asked, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Ruoyan. Xuansha said, "What words did he use to instruct his disciples?
The monk recounted the previous conversation. Xuansha remarked, "It is all the same—playing with the spirit—but it is truly extraordinary."
The Master said, "Strange! Why did you not simply remain there? The monk replied, "He has already passed away.
The Master asked, "Can he still be summoned to respond now? The monk was unable to answer.
Jingqing asked, "Heaven cannot cover him; earth cannot support him. Is this not so? The Master said, "If it is so, then he is covered and supported.
Jingqing said, "If it is not so, how many times has Ruiyan suffered for it? The Master called himself Shiyan.

Once there were three monks whose foreign features were clear-cut and sharp, their eyes like flashing lightning. They stood side by side with their shoulders touching and feet together to pay their respects. The Master asked them:

"Where have you come from? [The monk] replied, "From India. [The Master] asked, "When did you depart? He replied, "I set out this morning and have just arrived. [The Master] asked, "Are you not weary?
He replied, "For the sake of the Dharma, I have forgotten weariness. [The Master] gazed at him intently; his feet were not touching the ground at all.

The Master ordered him to enter the hall and take his place in the upper row. The next morning, he suddenly vanished. Furthermore, once a village woman came to pay her respects. The Master said to her, "Do not..."
He prostrated himself and hurried home to save several hundred lives. When the old woman returned, she saw her daughter-in-law just then gathering field snails;
the old woman immediately threw herself into the water [to save her]. Furthermore, several households invited him for a vegetarian feast (*śrāddha*); he arrived at each one simultaneously.
Finally, during the cremation, a giant serpent leapt from the treetop into the mass of flames. When the firewood was exhausted, the *śarīra* (relics) scattered and flew about, carried by the wind.
It stirred the grasses and trees, which fell down in profusion. The records of this Master’s miraculous manifestations throughout his life are beyond recounting.
▲ Chan Master Daoxian of Luoshan in Fuzhou asked Shishuang, "What is it like when arising and ceasing never cease? Shishuang replied, "One must become like cold ashes and withered wood;
one must go where a single thought lasts ten thousand years; one must reach the state where the box and its lid meet perfectly; one must be entirely pure."

He went to Juedian, but the Master did not approve. He then visited Yantou and asked the same question as before. Yantou shouted, "Who is it that arises and ceases? At this, the Master had an awakening.
While the Master was at Heshan, he saw off the elder Gu, his traveling companion, as they were leaving the gate.
He brandished his staff before him and cast it down. Gu had no reply. The Master said, "A stone ox blocks the ancient road; one horse gives birth to two."
Later, a monk cited this to Shushan. Shushan said, "A stone ox blocks the ancient road; one horse gives birth to three tigers.
Baofu asked, "Yantou said, 'In this way, in that way; not in this way, not in that way. What is the meaning of this?"
The Master called for Fú. Fú responded with an assent. The Master said, "Both are bright, and both are dark. Fú bowed in thanks.
Three days later, he asked again, "The other day I received the Master’s compassion, yet I simply could not see through it. The Master said, "I have told you everything there is to say.
Fú said, "The Master is like one carrying a torch while walking through the mountains. The Master said, "If that is so, then according to where you are still in doubt—"
The monk Jianglai asked Fú, "What is it like when both are illuminated and both are dark? Fú said, "Born together and dying together. Fú then bowed in thanks and withdrew.
Later, another monk asked Fú, "What is it like when born together and dying together?
Fú said, "I'll shut both dogs' mouths for you. The monk said, "Master, keep your mouth for eating your own rice. That monk then questioned [Fú again].

The Master said, "What is it like when those born together also die together? The Master replied, "Like a cow without horns. [The student] asked, "What is it like when those born together do not die together?
The Master replied, "Like a tiger with horns."
Later, a monk asked Zhaoqing. Zhaoqing said, "Both parties know each other. Why?
If I utter a single phrase on Pūrvavideha Island in the east, it will be known on Aparagoyānī Island in the west. If I utter a single phrase in the heavens, it will be known among humans.
Mind knows mind; eye illuminates eye."
The Master was traveling through Zhangzhou when he saw an inscription on the monument for Sanping, which said:
"When the Venerable One passed away, the assembly requested Han (name lost) to serve as the chief mourner. Han took a hand-towel and covered a gong with it;

he then placed a sharp-edged sword across the gong and, proceeding directly to the front of the shrine, set it down and asked: 'Is there anyone who can provide an answer? If you can, [then take this sword and strike the gong!']"
The man replied, "I shall act as the presiding mourner. If you cannot explain it, I will not. "Speak! Speak! [the Master said]. The assembly had no reply.
Han then kicked away the gong and wailed, "Heaven! Heaven! My late teacher is far gone! The Master said, "Alas, how extraordinary! How extraordinary!
The six hundred disciples under Sanping have all been swallowed up by this worldly fellow. Chen Lao.
If the Master had been present at that time, he would not have let him off so easily. At that moment, a monk asked: "If someone were to approach in such a manner, how would you respond?

The Master said: "If I had been there at that time, I would have simply covered my head with a three-foot square of cloth, slung a sharp-edged blade across my shoulder, lifted the mourning curtain with my hand, and sat right there in the doorway to watch this fellow from the Han family."
Han: "I cannot yet accept being the presiding mourner, nor can I yet refuse to be the presiding mourner. To advance, there must be propriety;
to retreat, there must be propriety."
Huanji asked, "Are the eyebrows there or not?

When the Master was first entering his residence at Luoshan, as he stepped onto the platform for the formal lecture, he merely gathered his robes and, just as he was about to sit, said, "Take care," and immediately descended from the seat.
After a long pause, he turned back and said, "Those who have not yet recognized [me], come forward. At that moment, a monk just stepped out to bow when the Master—
[The Master] said, "Oh, what great suffering! The monk rose from his prostrations and said, "I, [Name], ask the Master. The Master immediately shouted and sent him out.

A monk asked, "What is the extraordinary phrase? The Master said, "Say something! After a long silence, he said, "If one is a superior man, as soon as they step across the threshold, they will understand.
If you must present it face-to-face, you are still a dullard, babbling away with your mouth."
It does not take more than a single stroke of the mattock. Do you understand? It is not Zen, it is not the Way; it is not the Buddha, it is not the Dharma. What is it?
It is the wondrously sharp precious sword, ever manifest before one. It can kill, and it can also give life. If you can wield it, wield it as you please.
But if you wish to emerge from the fray and settle the matter, you must be such a man. Each and every opportunity [of the mind] must meet [the truth].
Sub-section: Dharmas have no root; they act as guest and host to one another. Even so, you must by all means avoid taking this upon yourself. Why?
If you let out the howl of a jackal, I shall roar the lion’s roar; if I let out the howl of a jackal, you too shall roar the lion’s roar.
If you roar the lion’s roar, I too shall roar the lion’s roar. At the moment of need, you must deploy these intentional phrases with mastery. Therefore—
The Way. The phrase within the mind; the mind within the phrase. The mind does not abide in the phrase; the phrase does not abide in the mind.

Mind and phrase are of different orders—how can one understand this? The mind can eradicate the phrase; the phrase can eradicate the mind. When mind and phrase race against one another, it is truly fearsome.
If mind and phrase are not clear, and principle and phenomenon do not penetrate, it is merely a "spearhead with no hole. Thus spoke the ancients.
To call such a person a "vulgar master" is like describing rice, hemp, bamboo, and reeds—what use are they?
Within this gate, one must be a true man of character. With eyes wide open and piercing, one turns with effortless agility upon being struck.
How could it be a matter of your being clear or turbid, or of what ordinary or holy beings can describe? When such a man of superior caliber meets another, it is like striking [a bell].
A spark from flint; like the crackling pattern on a tortoise shell. Rapid as the wind, swift in eloquence as lightning, it strikes with brilliant clarity.
Whether by one person or half a person, the matter is stripped away from words and phrases, yet its movement exceeds ten trillion. To lower the head and study Chan, one will ultimately not attain it.
Therefore, it is said: "In this way, it is easy; in another way, it is difficult. It is also said: "In this way, it is difficult; in another way, it is..."
"What do you all say to this? You must be extremely careful, brothers. Now, when traveling on pilgrimage, you must bring your eyes with you;
do not let yourselves be shrouded by such people as these. They will try to make you go off in total darkness, or make you go along in a state of dull stagnation. How bitter it is!"
To be thus obstructed and unjustly shackled—what end can there be? This fellow is like a gourd upon the water;
can anyone press it down? It is constantly manifest before one, flowing freely and at ease;
not a single dharma can cover it, nor can a single dharma equal it. As soon as it is touched, it reveals itself. Touch it...
As soon as it is encountered, it turns and rolls; it covers both sound and form. When unfolded, it circulates everywhere without obstruction, constantly revealed before one’s eyes.
How could it be something dull and stagnant? When it emerges, there is nothing that is not it; when it enters, every single thing returns to the source.

Before the sound, it stands solitary and distinct—how could it fall into the duality of existence and non-existence? Therefore it is said: "The single phrase prior to sound is not transmitted except by the Sages. It has never been personally...
Near, yet as if separated by a great trichiliocosm; a single thought prior to the sound—everyone knows this. How do you understand it? It is commonly said:
"Before the sound there is a path, which you must clearly penetrate through. "After the phrase it does not come" still leaves one half deficient.

If even a hair’s breadth is not penetrated, it is as if separated by the Iron Ring Mountains. Meeting such a marvel, with what will you respond? Generally, in proclaiming the Teaching, one must understand.
At present, regarding the phrases of life and death and the principles of killing and enlivening, one may then offer praise.

The "sword that kills" and the "sword that gives life" are the critical pivot of the ancients and likewise the essential core of the present day. To subdue demons and shatter attachments, they cannot be dispensed with;

to directly reveal the true teaching, one must know they are already possessed. That which is truly capable of breaking through possesses the great function without deficiency, and when perfect penetration manifests before one, demonic obstacles [are naturally overcome].
How can one find a foothold? If you have not yet attained such a state, how can you manifest it within all four modes of deportment?
Do you still see his face? Here, it is commonly said: "A single thought at the gate of the face is constant and uninterrupted.
Do you people attain this as well? If you have not truly clarified it, you must first stand forth for yourself, starkly naked. Do not...

It dwells as a neighbor to the myriad dharmas; yet it cannot be covered by any dharma whatsoever. Thus, the ancients said: "There is no dharma before the eyes, yet the meaning lies right before the eyes.
It is not a dharma of the present moment; it is not something reached by the ears or the eyes. First, one must cause fundamental wisdom (*mūla-jñāna*) to manifest.
Then the local scenery of the original ground will be constantly revealed—naked and bare, free and at ease, entering and exiting without obstruction.
Only when you are truly stuck can you then transgress the timing; even when the dragon spirits hold up flowers, there is no way through. When outsiders peek in secretly, they see not a trace.
This is not a matter of merely obliterating form, yet it is indeed going. Brothers, you must penetrate to the very top and to the very bottom before you attain it.

Do not merely dabble here and there, seizing a few fragments of words and phrases, inserting remarks at various places, pointing east and drawing west, citing the ancients and the present—this merely serves to obstruct.
"Paṇḍita! What crime is there in killing ten thousand people with a mallet? Tomorrow or the day after, we shall cast men and women of your household into irons and hammers;
the day will come when we beat the ghost-bone buttocks of you lot. Do you understand? The profundity of the Zen school must be measured within one's own breast."

Coarse food brings quick satiety; slow chewing prevents hunger. That the root causes differ is entirely due to one's own errors. To labor in vain for this single lifetime, with an empty stomach and a haughty heart—who else is to blame for such faults?
One merely consumes the words of others, picking and choosing between right and wrong, while occupying oneself solely with one’s own strengths.
This is absolutely impossible. "Take care," he said, as he was about to pass away. He ascended the hall to gather the assembly; after a long silence, he extended his left hand.
The attendants did not know what to do, so he ordered the monks on the eastern side to step back. He then extended his right hand and ordered the monks on the western side to step back.
He then said, "To repay the Buddha’s kindness, nothing surpasses the circulation of the Great Teaching. Now, you may go."
"Go back now. Take care. Having spoken these words, he smiled gently and passed away.
Chan Master Shibi Zongyi of Xuansha in Fuzhou was the son of the Xie family from Min County, Fuzhou.
In his youth, he fished on the banks of the Nantai River. Upon reaching maturity, he suddenly abandoned his boat and followed Chan Master Lingxun of Mount Furong to have his hair shaved.

He went to the Vinaya Master Kaiyuan Tongxuan at Nanchang and received full ordination. Wearing straw sandals and cloth robes, he took only enough food to sustain his breath, sitting in meditation all day long;
the assembly marveled at him. Initially, he had treated Xuefeng as his elder brother, but later he became his disciple.
Because of his ascetic practices, Xuefeng called him "Dhuta. One day, Xuefeng asked, "Which one is Dhuta Bei? The Master replied: [He pointed to himself.]
He replied, "I shall never dare to deceive others. On another day, Feng summoned him, saying, "Head-tato Bei, why do you not go to study under various masters?
The Master said, "Bodhidharma did not come to this eastern land; the Second Patriarch did not go to the Western Heaven. Feng approved of this.

When they ascended Mount Xianggu, he and the Master worked together to establish the monastery. As disciples arrived in great numbers, the Master entered the inner quarters to seek resolution from the Master, never failing to do so.

From dawn until dusk, he further studied the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* and realized the nature of the mind-ground. Consequently, his responses to the needs of others were swift and nimble, and his understanding was in profound accord with the *Sūtras*.
Whenever scholars from various regions encountered points they could not resolve, they invariably sought instruction from him.
Even when engaging in rigorous inquiry with Xuefeng, he did not shrink from the responsibility of a benevolent teacher. Xuefeng remarked, "Tou-tuo Bei is a man who has returned for a second birth."
The *Zhengfayan zang* states: Initially, wishing to travel extensively through all directions to seek out spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), he took his bag and crossed the mountain ridges.
He stubbed his toe, and blood flowed with excruciating pain. He sighed and said, "This body does not truly exist; from where does this pain arise?
Thereupon, he returned to Xuefeng.

Xuefeng ascended the hall and said, "To understand this matter, it is like an ancient mirror set upon its stand: when a barbarian comes, a barbarian appears; when a Han person comes, a Han person appears.
A monk came forward from the assembly and asked, "What happens when a bright mirror arrives? Xuefeng replied, "Both the barbarian and the Han person are hidden.
The monk said, "The old monk’s feet have not yet touched the ground. Xuefeng pointed to the fire and said, "Three..."
"The Buddhas of the world turn the Great Dharma Wheel within a mass of flames. The Master said, "Lately the King’s decrees have become somewhat strict. Feng asked, "How so?
The Master said, "They do not permit anyone to jostle others or snatch goods from the marketplace."
Yunmen said, "The flames preach the Dharma for the Buddhas of the three periods of time; the Buddhas of the three periods stand upon the ground and listen.
Huanglong Xin remarked, "Xuefeng and Yunmen vie with one another for brilliance. When the fuel is exhausted and the fire is extinguished, where do the Buddhas of the three periods go to listen?
Do not linger sitting in the depths of white clouds; take care not to be burned by cold ashes."
[He] killed a person.
While traveling with Xuefeng, as they were walking through the mountains, Xuefeng pointed to the ground before them and said, "On this plot of land, one could build a seamless stupa.
The Master asked, "How high would it be? Xuefeng looked up and down. The Master said, "The merit and retribution of humans and devas..."
"Not non-existent. "If you were one who received the prediction at Vulture Peak, you have not even dreamed of it.
Xuefeng asked, "And what about you? The Master said, "Seven feet, eight feet. Xuefeng said, "The world is one foot wide;
the ancient mirror is one foot wide. The world is ten feet wide; the ancient mirror is ten feet wide. The Master pointed to the brazier and said, "How wide is this brazier?"
[Shao] said, "It is as wide as an ancient mirror. The Master said, "The old monk’s heels have not yet touched the ground.
While [the Master] was with Xuefeng by a bamboo fence, he asked, "Is there Buddha-dharma even in this place by the bamboo fence? Xuefeng said, "There is.
The Master asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma in this place by the bamboo fence? Xuefeng shook the fence once. The Master said, "I do not agree with that."
Xuefeng said, "How about you? The Master said, "It comes through the end of the bamboo strips. The Master took his leave of Xuefeng, saying, "I inform the Abbot:
every person is free and at ease. I am now going down the mountain. Xuefeng asked, "Who says such a thing?
The Master said, "It is the Abbot who says such a thing. Xuefeng asked, "What about you? The Master said: [He remained silent.]
"Not free and at ease. Fengyun Zhi. Xuefeng said to the Master, "There is an Elder Nanji who has questions for which there is no answer that can be given.
One day Nanji arrived at Xuefeng’s place, and Xuefeng ordered him to visit the Master. The Master said, "An ancient said, 'In this matter, only I can know it.
Elder, what do you say? Nanji replied, "One must know that which does not seek."
When asked about this, the Master said, "What is the old fellow on the mountain head doing, undergoing all this hardship?
Daowei Zhenru cited this, saying: "Xuansha spoke thus; Daowei cited it thus. One must not move a muscle. Why?
It is like striking a 'poisoned drum': those who hear it, whether far or near, all perish."
When the Master saw a monk coming to prostrate, he said: "Go ahead and prostrate; it is because of me that you may pay homage to you.
Jingshan Daoyuan’s verse says: "The Master did not know characters; Bodhidharma did not understand Chan.
Xuansha had no such words— Do not recklessly transmit them."
A monk asked, "What is the student's own self? The Master said, "What use have you for your own self?
Yunmen remarked, "A man of immeasurable capacity has been turned around by the flow of words. The monk then followed up by asking Yunmen, "What is the student's own self?
Yunmen said, "Suddenly, someone on the road calls out to the monk, 'Come to the meal! You too—"
He ate the rice as it was served.
Gushan arrived; the Master drew a circle and showed it to him. Gushan said, "Everyone is unable to get out of this.
The Master said, "I knew you would be making your living in the belly of a donkey or a horse. Gushan asked, "And what about you, Preceptor?"
Sheng said, "Everyone can produce this, yet they cannot get out of it. Shanshan said, "The Master can speak thus, but why can I not?
The Master said, "I can, but you cannot. The King of Min sent lychees to the Master.
The Master picked one up and showed it to the assembly, saying, "This lychee is so red! This lychee..."
"It is so very red! How do you all understand this? If you say it is 'one color,' you are still muddled;
if you say it is 'many colors,' you fall into the extremes of annihilationism or eternalism. How will you deal with this? A monk stepped forward and said, "One cannot fail to recognize the lychee.
The Master spoke on his behalf, saying, "It is simply a lychee."

"A student of the Way must employ the unchanging pivot in the midst of activity. Yet, even those who have spent their lives in the monastic forests fail to recognize these words—how lamentable!
Xuan Sha once ate lychees and asked the assembly, "This lychee is so red; this is so crimson.
How do you all understand this? If you say it is a single color, that is still a state of stagnation.

[The monk] said, "One cannot fail to recognize the *lìzhī* (lychee). Xuansha said, "It is simply the *lìzhī*.
He further said, "All of you have been with me for so long, yet you all speak in this manner; you do not distinguish between the black and the white, nor do you recognize good and ill fortune.

[The Master] said: "What negotiation is there? Chan Master Daohui said: "The former sages, pitying you for your inverted and frantic pursuits, provided a single phrase to bring about liberation.

instead, exert some effort yourself and respond from within the pivot of the dialogue. To take this 'head-word' (huatou) as the Way of Chan is not only to deceive yourself, but also..."

Once the newcomer has completed the formalities of deportment, he himself strikes the *pǔqǐng* drum three times and then enters the Sangha Hall.
After some time, he reports to the Master, saying, "The newcomer has slighted the Venerable One. The Master says, "Strike the bell to assemble the community for an interrogation.
When the assembly has gathered, the newcomer does not appear. The Master orders an attendant to go and summon him. As soon as the newcomer arrives at the Dharma Hall, he turns back toward—
The attendant patted him on the back and said, "The Master calls you. When the attendant reached the Master’s quarters, the newly arrived monk returned to the hall.
The long-resident monk asked, "Why did the Master not examine the newcomer? The Master replied, "I have already examined you.
While they were working together gathering firewood, they saw a tiger. Tiantong said, "Master, it is a tiger! The Master said, "It is you."
After the tiger returned to the monastery, Tianlong asked, "Just now you saw the tiger and said it was you; I wonder what your intention was?
The Master replied, "In this Sahā world there are four kinds of most grave matters. If a person can penetrate them, they will be able to transcend the realm of shadows."
Miaoxi spoke on his behalf: "I know that the Master’s concern for others is earnest. Xuedou said:
"If you wish to act as a teacher to gods and men, there is truly a tiger right before you. Baoning Yong composed this verse: A fierce tiger stands in the path, alone displaying its majesty;

"How truly lamentable!

"Where have all the clamor and bustle of yesterday gone? Heaven shares its clarity with the white clouds at dawn; water flows with the bright moon."
