Propagating the Way depends on oneself; preaching the Dharma for others is difficult. Once you have attained clarity, it lies in putting it into practice. Generally speaking, this is the standard for all patriarchs.
He preached the Dharma: "Within a single phrase, the Three Mysteries are complete; within each Mystery, the Three Essentials are complete.

You have entered the realm of reality. Sit down, put on your robe, and look behind you; naturally, you shall go forth with the seven powers unobstructed and the eight directions open. The Master remained in attendance for another seven years.
He then took his leave. Han Zicang asked Dahui, "What do you think of Master Qing?
Dahui replied, "I have heard that when he cited the kōan of Layman Pang’s question to Mazu regarding 'not being a companion to the myriad dharmas,' he said: 'Fish, dragons, shrimp, and crabs.'"
"Where should it be placed? If it were like this, you would have obtained its name in vain. Zicang conveyed these words to the Master. The Master said, "Tell him:
'It is like one person traveling by boat and another traveling by land; both arrive at the same time.
When Hui heard these words, he said, "Cao Tang has attained it."
▲ Zen Master Weixin of Qingyuan in Jizhou ascended the hall and said: "When I was thirty years ago, before I had studied Zen, I saw mountains as mountains and waters as waters.
Later, when I encountered a true teacher and attained a point of entry, I saw mountains were not mountains and waters were not waters. Now, having attained a place of rest, it is just as before."
"Seeing a mountain as merely a mountain; seeing water as merely water. O Great Assembly, are these three kinds of insight the same or different?

If there is anyone among you who can distinguish them clearly, I grant that you have personally seen this old monk. (Even after thirty more years of further investigation, you will find no point of entry.)"
▲ Chan Master Benquan of Baofu in Zhangzhou. When Huang Shanggu first attained some realization, he asked Haitang, "Who here is capable of engaging in discourse with me?

Haitang replied, "Benquan of Zhangzhou. At that time, the Master was supervising laborers while they were clearing land for fields. Huang Shanggu went together with Haitang to visit him and posed this question:
"Does the *zhisui* (the temple official in charge of labor) know that the pillar has given birth to a child? The Master asked, "Is it a boy or a girl?"
Huang made a proposal, but the Master waved him away. Huang said, "You must not be so discourteous. The Master replied, "This blockhead!
If you do not strike him now, when will you? Huang laughed heartily. Ascending the hall, he cited a verse by Hanshan, saying: "My mind is like the autumn moon."
The emerald pool is clear and limpid; nothing can be compared to it. How am I to describe it? I, the old monk, am not like this. My mind is like a lantern:
when the flame is lit, it is red both inside and out. There is something that can be compared to it: tomorrow morning, the sun will rise in the east.

Those who transmitted the teachings took this as a joke. When Dashi Xian (Dead Heart) Zen Master saw it, he sighed and said, "If Brother Quan’s proclamations are such as these, he truly does not fail the entrustment of our former teacher."
▲ When the Layman Huang Tingjian of Taishi Shangu first visited Master Xiù Yuántong, their conversation is recorded in the chapter on Yuántong.

From that time on, he composed a text of vows and strictly abstained from alcohol and sexual indulgence. Eating only morning congee and midday rice, he applied himself with keen resolve to seeking the Way.
Having taken refuge under Huìtáng, he requested instruction on the direct and swift path. Huìtáng said: "As for what Confucius said: 'The disciples..."
"Do I hide anything from you? I do not hide anything from you. How would Grand Historian Juchang have explained this in his usual manner?

When Master Gong was about to offer a response, the Master said, "No, no. Gong remained in a state of persistent confusion. One day, while attending the Master as they were walking in the mountains, Gong asked:

At that time, the rock-orchids were in full bloom. The Hall Master asked, "Do you smell the fragrance of the *mugicha* (woodchrysanthemum)? The Official replied, "I do. The Hall Master said, "I have hidden nothing from you.
The Official felt relieved and immediately prostrated himself, saying, "How can the Master be so earnest with such a compassionate, grandmotherly heart?
The Hall Master smiled and said, "I only wish for you to reach home. After some time, he went to visit Chan Master Sixin Xin and entered the room with the assembly.
Xinjian opened his eyes wide and asked, "The New Elder has died; the Scholar has died. They have been burned into two heaps of ash.
Where will you meet them? Gong was speechless. Xinjian said to him, "What you have attained through your studies under Huitang has not yet taken effect.
Later, while serving as an official in Qian-nan, his power of the Way grew even more supreme. Within a state of non-thought, he suddenly realized the meaning of what Sijian had taught.

Question: In a letter sent in reply, he said: "In years past, I was repeatedly exhorted by you with great persistence. For a long time, I remained as if in a drunken dream, lingering vaguely within the realm of light and shadow.
This was because my doubts were not yet exhausted and the root of my life-destiny was not severed; thus, I retreated, turning back as if gazing at a precipice.
While on the road in Qian Nan during my exile, I woke from a midday nap and suddenly reflected: 'I have been deceived by the old monks of the world!'"
Most people have spent their lives on this; only the monk Sishin refused to do so, which was his primary way of acting for others’ benefit.
▲ The layman Wu Xun, a Secretariat scholar whose courtesy name was De-fu, visited Huìtáng.

Huìtáng said to him, “I shall not ask about the many interpretations, memories, and extensive learning you have acquired throughout your life. But tell me a single phrase from before your parents were even born. The official—
As he was about to speak, the Master struck him with his whisk. He immediately grasped the profound meaning and presented three verses in succession. The last of them read: "Ha!
This worldly fellow of much knowledge, Who has chewed through all ancient and modern koans, Suddenly, amidst a heap of scattered refuse, Picks up a dung-ball from a dung beetle.
It is plain and clear, not worth a single coin; Ten thousand taels of gold cannot buy it. I casually pick it up and show it to you."
People say it is simply because watching a spinning plate is difficult.
▲ Chan Master Doushuai Congyue of Longxing Prefecture was initially the head of the assembly at Daowu. Leading several monks, he went to visit Master Yungai Zhi.
Before Zhi had spoken more than a few sentences, he fully understood everything the master held within him. He then smiled and said, "I observe the head..."
The Master’s bearing was extraordinary; yet, how was it that his speech and breath were like those of a drunkard?

The Master felt his face flush and sweat break out, saying, “I pray that the Venerable One will not withhold his compassion. Zhi spoke with him again, piercing him with sharp words, until the Master was utterly bewildered.
He then requested to enter the room for instruction. Zhi asked, “Have you ever met Master Fachang Yu? The Master replied, “I have read his recorded sayings.”
“[I] understand; I do not wish to see him. Zhi said, “Have you ever seen Master Wenzhun of Dongshan?
The Master replied, “That man from Guansi has no sense at all. He drags around a hempen skirt and reeks of urine. What excellence does he have? Zhi said:
"You need only investigate by way of the stench of urine. Following these instructions, the Master went to see Dongshan, where he deeply grasped the profound essence of the teaching.

He then went to see Zhi, who asked, "Now that you have seen the man from Guansi, how is the Great Matter? The Master replied, "Had it not been for the Venerable’s guidance, I would have missed my entire life.
He then paid his respects and departed. The Master subsequently visited Zhenjing and later entered the world [as a teacher].
At the Deer Park, there was a man of pure and simple character who had long studied under Ciming. He lived in a single room and never initiated contact with others.

Once, while the Master was eating lychees preserved in honey, the man happened to pass by his door. The Master called out to him, saying, "These are the fruits of your native province; you may eat them with me.
The man replied, "Since the passing of my late teacher, I have not been able to eat these for a long time. The Master said, "My late teacher..."
"Who was it? Su asked. "It was Ciming," he replied. "I have been humbled by serving him for thirteen years.
The Master was struck with wonder and said, "To endure the toil of service for thirteen years—how could this be anything other than having attained the Way? He then offered him some leftover fruit.
He gradually grew more intimate with him. Su asked, "Whom did your teacher see? The Master replied, "Dongshan Wen. Su asked, "Whom did Wen see?

The Master replied, "Huanglong Nan. Su remarked, "Nan the Junior was under my late teacher; it was not long before his Dharma path flourished in such a manner. The Master became even more astonished and fearful.
He then placed incense in his sleeve and went to pay his respects to Su. Su rose and stepped aside to avoid him, saying, "I—"
Because his merit was thin, his former master had given him a prediction that he would not be permitted to become a human being. The Master [Zhaozhou] became even more reverent.

Xisu then said, "I pity your sincerity, yet it contravenes my former master’s prediction. Try telling me what you have attained throughout your life. The Master fully explained everything he had perceived.
Xisu said, "You can enter the Buddha, but you cannot enter Māra. The Master asked, "What do you mean by this? Xisu replied, "Have you not seen..."
An ancient said: "The final phrase is where one first reaches the secure gate. After [Wen] had been thus for several days, Su finally granted him certification (*inka*).
He then cautioned him, saying: "What I have shown you are all matters of right knowledge and right view. However, because you left your teacher too early, you were unable to exhaust its subtlety.
I shall now pierce through this for you, so that you may attain great mastery in its application. On a future day, you must..."

"Do not succeed me. After the Master [Fengxue] succeeded Zhenjing, he acted in accordance with what had been previously cautioned. In his quarters, the Master established three questions to test his students. The first was:
"One brushes away the weeds and gazes at the wind, seeking only to see one's nature. Where, then, is the nature of this very person? The second was:
"Once you have recognized your own nature, you will be liberated from birth and death. When the light of the eyes falls to the ground, what then?"

"Third, regarding liberation from birth: once one has attained liberation from birth and death, one immediately knows the destination. When the four great elements separate, to what place does one go?
Zhang Wujin answered these three questions with verses. The first said: "In the dense shade of summer trees, the cuckoo cries; the sun—"
The floating clouds are shattered and the universe is clear. Do not face Zeng Shen’s question regarding Zeng Xi;

from of old, a filial son has avoided his father’s name. The second verse says: A ghost messenger from the human world arrives with a summons; the color of the flower-crown in the heavens is already fading.
What a fine moment for a turning over—do not let Old Yan know of it too easily. The third verse says: The drums beat together in the east...

The wife of Li of the village; in the vast wilderness of the western wind, tears drench her robes. Upon the southern bank of the Yangtze, where green reeds and red smartweed grow, she has instead become Zhang San, sitting upon a fishing rock.
In the winter of the sixth year of the Yuanyou era, having finished her bath, she gathered the assembly and spoke this verse: "Forty-eight years old—saints and commoners alike have been slain."
Not a hero. The road at Long’an is slippery. Suddenly, he passed away.
▲ Zen Master Fozhao Gaofeng of Fayun Temple in Dongjing visited Zen Master Yuan Tong Ji. During their private interview, Ji raised the following case:
A monk asked Touzi, “When a person who has died the great death comes back to life, what then? Touzi said, “I do not permit you to travel by night.”
"At dawn we must arrive. What is your intention? The Master replied, "The debt is too great to repay. Yuan Tong highly praised this.
A few days later, when the ceremony for appointing a monk to wield the whisk was being held, [Yuan Tong’s] thoughts were sluggish and dull, causing the entire hall to burst into loud laughter.

The Master felt ashamed. The following day, he specially prepared tea for the assembly; as he placed the tea service on the table, he felt so ashamed he did not know how to comport himself. By chance, he struck...

While overturning tea utensils, his ladle fell to the ground and hopped several times. At that moment, he attained awakening and realized the answer; his spiritual acuity was so swift that none dared to confront him.
He then went to the place of Zhenjing, where, while contemplating a verse by the Patriarch, he read: "The mind is identical to the realm of empty space; it manifests dharmas equal to empty space.
When one realizes empty space, there is neither 'is' nor 'is not. At this, he attained a sudden and great enlightenment. Thereafter, he appeared in the world [to teach].
At that time, while giving a small-scale sermon upon ascending the hall, he often said to people:
"In the third year of the Shaosheng era, on the twenty-first day of the eleventh month, our Master attained the Chan of the 'square inch' (the mind). He also said:

'In the third year of the Xining era, our Master’s official documents were submitted at Fengxiang Prefecture; that very year, eighteen prefectures of Huashan were lost. You lot—eggplants and gourds—what do you know?"
From this, one comes to understand. Someone asked: "On the Lion Throne of King Ratnakusuma, why is it always the conventional truth? The Master said:
"Foolish man, how could there be two kinds of Buddha-nature?"
The *Dahui Zongmen Wuku* states: Chan Master Fayun Fozhao Gaofeng once retired to the Iron Arhat Hall at Jingde Monastery.
In the hall were several wooden arhats; as the capital suffered from bitter cold, Gaofeng took them and burned them, sitting by the brazier until dawn.
The following day, he retrieved countless śarīra relics from the ashes. The various presiding masters...
His contemporaries all regarded him as a follower of external paths (*tīrthika*). This was because Fozhao belonged to the lineage of Danxia;

he was not someone that could be verified by the eyes of the mundane. It is further said: When the Venerable Fozhao Gaofeng first resided at Guizong, he applied himself with singular devotion to the practice of the Way, never for a moment slackening.
Late one night, after completing his ritual prostrations, he sat within the floor-heater (*dilu*) of the monks' hall. Suddenly, he saw two monks.
They entered the hall. One was a man with a thick, bushy beard and hair as white as snow; the other was a youth, both possessing tall and elegant statures.
Daogao felt joyful in his heart and said to himself, "In my assembly there are monks such as these. After a short while, the two men left the hall.
Daogao followed behind them and saw them enter the Buddha Hall. He also followed them inside. The light from the lamps flickered brightly, and there was still incense smoke rising from the burner.

The fire was bright as he offered incense and prostrated before the Buddha. Two monks emerged once more, following closely behind him. Upon reaching the front of the Buddha Hall, they suddenly lost his whereabouts.
He thought to himself that he had forgotten the incense box inside the hall. As he turned back to retrieve it, he saw that the hall door was locked.
He then called for the attendant, the monk Shoushun, to open the door. Shun took the key and opened the door; when he looked inside—
The incense smoke in the burner had not yet dissipated, and the incense casket remained upon the jeweled steps; he himself could not explain the reason for this.
Miaoxi personally saw Fozhao speak of it, and at that time Shoushun was standing nearby, still pointing to him as a witness.

▲ When Chan Master Létán Zhàntáng Wénzhǔn of Lóngxīng Prefecture first visited Chan Master Shèng of Liāngshān, Shèng said, "Before you have received the full precepts, how dare you study the Buddha-vehicle?
The Master pressed his palms together and said, "Is the ordination platform itself the precepts?"

When the Karmadāna and the Brahma-carya Ācārya were about to confer the precepts, the Master was greatly startled. The Preceptor laughed and said, "Even so, how could I dare not receive your instruction?
Thereupon, he received the full ordination from Vinaya Master Tang’an. Having paid his respects to Zhenjing, Zhenjing asked, "Where have you recently departed from?
The Master replied, "Dayang. [Zhenjing] asked, "Where did you spend the summer retreat? The Master replied, "Dawei. [Zhenjing] asked, "Where are you from?"
The Master said, “Xingyuanfu. Jìng spread out his hands and asked, “How is my hand like the Buddha’s hand? The Master was at a loss.
Jìng said, “Just now, when you were responding to each question, everything was luminous and each thing was true to its nature.
Yet, as soon as you spoke of ‘my hand being like the Buddha’s hand,’ it became an obstruction. Tell me, where does the sickness lie? The Master said, “I do not understand. Jìng said, “One—”

Everything was fully realized; whom else could he have been taught to understand? The Master [Dongshan] submitted himself to him and joined the ranks of his disciples for over ten years, following him wherever he went.
In the third year of the Zhenxing era, when Zhenjing moved to Shimen, the number of *nàzǐ* (patch-robed monks) increased even further.

Whenever anyone entered the inner chamber to pose a question, he would sit upright with eyes closed and offer no instruction. Upon seeing those who came to study, he would go to tend the vegetable garden; this became his constant practice.

Changshi said to his fellow practitioner, the Venerable Gong: "Does this old man have no interest in the Way of the Dharma? One day, while raising his staff to clear a drainage ditch, water splashed onto his robes;
he suddenly attained great enlightenment and rushed to recount the matter. Jing scolded him, saying: "Is this the kind of reckless, vulgar behavior you dare to display?
From then on, his traces became even more hidden, yet his fame grew ever greater. Initially, when Yunyan’s seat was vacant, the Prefect ordered [him to take it].
Master Sishin cited someone he knew. Xinxin said, "Zhun the Mountain Master is capable of holding this position, though I have never met him.
I have seen a verse he wrote on washing a bowl that is quite excellent. Muxi requested him to recite it. Sishin recited: "The 'zhi', 'hu', 'ye', and 'ra'—the nostrils of the patch-robed monk."
His large head hung downward. If you still do not understand, go ask Old Woman Wang of the Eastern Village. This was a marvel. He went to invite Master Yunyan [to take charge];
later, when the Master was appointed as Abbot of Yunyan, Xinxin said to Zhang Bangchang, the Temple Administrator:
"This elder has a most formidable nose. One day, while he was presiding over a gathering of monks from various mountains at Nanchang, the Master arrived late. Xinxin pointed [at him] and said:

[The Master] said, "This monk from the river valley even breaks the phrasing when responding; yet he dares to come out and act as an elder. The Master gave a shout and said, "When did you ever break the phrasing?
He looked at Xinggu and said, "I told you he has nostrils. Xinggu was greatly pleased. One day, a newly arrived monk came for an audience.
As he spread his sitting cloth, the Master said, "Before you have completed your formal greetings, where have you recently departed from, Upādhyāya?"
[The monk] said, "Lu Shan Guizong. The Master asked, "Where does the 'Patriarch' (Zong) return? [The monk] said, "Aha! The Master said, "Making a living inside a toad's den.
[The monk] said, "Why do you not understand my words? The Master said, "Do you not yourself come from Guizong? [The monk] said, "Yes.
The Master said, "A fellow who follows behind donkeys and horses. Then he questioned the second seat: "Where have you recently departed from? [He] said, "Yuanzhou."
The Master asked, "Where have you been this summer? The monk replied, "At Mount Yang. The Master said, "Did you see Little Śākyamuni? The monk replied, "I saw him.
The Master asked, "How long are his nostrils? The monk hesitated. The Master said, "The teacher has dropped the talk. [Another] monk asked, "What have you come for?
The monk replied, "I have come specifically to pay my respects to the Master. The Master said, "Clouds at the mountain peak are never idle; water..."
As the mountain stream flowed down the ravine, [the Master] said, "It is far too busy for you to be born here. The monk said, "Master, do not deceive people.
The Master said, "Why did Master Mazu pass right under your feet, O *śrāmaṇera*? The monk was speechless. The Master said, "In fact, it is you who are deceiving this old monk.
One day, in the Dharma Hall, he encountered the Head Seat and asked, "Where are you going? The Seat said, "I am about to—"
The Master said, "I wish to discuss a matter with you. The monk replied, "Please do so. The Master said, "The ladle handle of the eastern neighbor is long;
the ladle handle of the western neighbor is short. The monk asked, "Why is it that you pick up a tea pitcher from Gong County, yet serve from a porcelain bowl from Raozhou?

The Master said, "Looking down at the river from the edge of a cliff—one needlessly brings about a scene of sorrow. The monk cried out in protest. The Master stuck out his tongue and withdrew. A monk asked, "The Teachings..."
“Regarding the Middle Way: if there is a person who gives rise to true realization and returns to the source, the empty space of the ten directions will all vanish and dissolve.
I do not yet understand how this principle works. The Master then opened his palms and pointed his fingers, saying: “Zi, Chou, Yin, Mao, Chen, Si, Wu, Wei;
one Luo, two Tu, three Shui, four Jin, five Taiyang, six Taiyin, seven Jidu. Today it is Jidu.”
The stars enter the House of Cancer. Baofeng does not beat this drum or blow this flute; he then descends from his seat. Entering the hall: "Five nines make forty-five.
The Sage acts and all things behold him. In the Qin era, the carriage wheel passed over the sharp tip of the drill-bit;
before the Han Emperor’s hall, Fan Kuai was just like that. I have heard that on Yellow Crane Tower, Cui Hao composed a poem upon its summit: "The clear river stretches clearly..."
The trees of Hanyang; the fragrant grasses grow lushly on Parrot Isle (*Píngyǔ Zhōu*). One may know the rites (*lǐ*) here. "The gentleman applies himself to the root.

When the root is established, the Way (*dào*) arises. The Way gives birth to One; One gives birth to Two; Two give birth to Three; Three give birth to the myriad things. [The Master] suddenly picks up his staff, stands up, and says:
"O Assembly! How does Baofeng compare to Confucius? After a long silence, he says: "When wine meets a kindred spirit, it is drunk."
"A poem is recited for one who understands. [The Master] struck his staff and descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, he issued this notice: "It has rained continuously without clearing;
it has become such that black clouds gather thickly atop Mount Wulao, and white waves surge to the heavens within Lake Dongting.
Great Master Yunmen, unable to restrain his impatience, burns incense within the Buddha Hall and joins his palms at the main gate, offering prayers and vows: 'May...'"
The stone woman of Huangmei gives birth to a child; mother and child are complete and whole. The hornless iron ox of Shaoshi always delights in water and grass.
[The Master] lets out a shout and says, "What connection is there? He then looks at the assembly and says, "Were it not for Yang Deyi, who would have seen Ma Xiangru?
The Master returned from Zhejiang to Leshan Tan and paid his respects to Chan Master Shen (who was also a successor of Zhenjing). Soon thereafter, he was ordered to share the seat [with the Master].

There was a monk named Wengu who, upon seeing the remains of kitchen scraps thrown away, attained realization. He went to the Abbot’s quarters to communicate his awakening, but the Master shouted deeply at him and sent him out.
Consequently, Wengu lost his resolve and hanged himself in the latrine of the Yanshou Hall. Thereafter, he appeared and disappeared without a fixed time, and the community feared him.

The Master intentionally went to the toilet in the middle of the night; just as he was removing his robes, Wengu immediately arrived carrying pure water. The Master said, "Wait for me to finish undressing."
When the robes had been removed, Wuzhuo returned. Before long, he was serving the counting sticks. After the Master had finished washing them, he called for Wuzhuo to take away the rinsing bucket.
As soon as Wuzhuo took it, the Master grasped his hand and asked, "Are you the attendant Wuzhuo? Wuzhuo replied, "Yes. The Master said:
"Was there someone at that time in the guest prefect’s quarters who, upon seeing a falling match-head, attained enlightenment?

In Zen practice and the study of the Way, one seeks only to know the place where one's own 'original source' (the *benming yuanchen*) falls. You have needlessly made such a distinction between going and staying."
When you moved the head seat’s sandals in the treasury hall, was that not what you realized at that time?
When you moved the pillow in the guest prefect’s quarters, was that not what you realized at that time?
Every night you were here moving water and counting tally-sticks; was that not what you realized at that time? Why do you not know where it has gone, yet...
He was causing disturbances here among the assembly. The Master pushed him away with great force, and he let out a hollow, rattling sound.

From that point on, he vanished without a trace. Throughout his life, the Master disciplined himself with austerity; even while leading disciples and propagating the Dharma, he did not differ from when he was among the common assembly.

After rising in the morning, he would go to the rack and take only a small ladle of hot water to wash his face, using the remainder to wash his feet. His other uses of resources were for the most part similar to this.

After the evening session had concluded, the attendants of the abbot’s quarters and the laborers were like strangers to him; he personally performed all tasks, such as sweeping the floor and brewing tea.
In the summer of the fifth year of the Zhenghe era, the Master fell ill. Those who brought him medicine instructed him to avoid toxic substances, but the Master would not comply.
Someone asked him the reason for this. The Master said, "Does illness have an inherent nature? The man replied, "No.
The Master said, "Since it has no inherent nature, I am using emptiness to accommodate emptiness; I have never been inverted. The Head Seat asked, "How is your health these days, Master?
The Master said, "A lame donkey climbing a wall. The Head Seat said, "Master, you too should take a dose of medicine. The Master said, "Building a bridge over rotten wood."
[The Master] said, "I know you, Reverend, do not understand the need for dietary restraint. The Master asked, "How about you?
As the monk was about to offer a reply, the Master said, "You, too, should take a dose of medicine. On the twentieth day of the seventh month, he changed his robes, recited a verse, and passed away.
Upon cremation, *śarīra* were obtained—crystal-clear, round, and lustrous; his eyes, teeth, and rosary remained unburnt. He was enshrined in a stupa on the southern slope of the mountain.

▲ Chan Master Juefan Huihong of Qingliang in Ruizhou was the son of the Peng family of that prefecture. Having lost his father at a young age, he became a novice under Chan Master Qingsong of Sanfeng.
He could memorize several thousand words a day. At nineteen, he passed the scriptural examination and received full ordination.
For four years, he followed Master Xuanmi to study the *Satyasiddhi-śāstra* and the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra*. Thereafter, he left them to visit Zhenjing at Guizong. When Zhenjing moved...

At Shimen, the Master followed him there. Jìng was troubled by the depth and obscurity of the teachings he heard, and he frequently raised the words of Xuansha regarding "not yet having reached the ultimate" to express his doubts.
Whenever [the Master] offered a response, Jìng would say, "Are you again expounding upon principles? One day, he suddenly cast off all his doubts and composed a verse, saying:
"Once Lingyun saw it, he did not see it again; On every branch, red and white, no flowers cling. How vexing!"
"A guest on a fishing boat comes instead to the level ground to scoop up fish and shrimp. Jingjian expressed his joy at this.
The *Zhizhengchuan* states: "In the past, I was dwelling in a hermitage beneath Jiufeng in Gaoyang. A monk asked me:"
In the assembly of Linji, two monks once met and simultaneously let out a shout. Hearing this, Linji ascended the seat and said, "O Great Assembly!
If you wish to understand the Linji phrase of guest and host, go ask the two Zen practitioners in the hall.
A monk then asked, "Which one is the guest? Which one is the host? Linji replied, "Guest and host are clearly distinct. I, Yu Fang, [have recorded this].
Desiring to repay [his teacher], he suddenly perceived the essential principles of the Three Mysteries and the Three Essentials. Thereupon, he prostrated himself twice and said:

"How magnificent is the banner of non-action and quiescent extinction! Even if there were those who heard of it throughout hundreds or thousands of generations, their thieving minds would be utterly extinguished;
how much more so for me, who lived some two hundred years after the Great Master? I shall compose a verse, saying: Within a single phrase, the three gates of mystery are complete."
Within the single mystery, the three essential paths are complete; examine them closely, and they are the very trap for tigers. Suddenly, with a thunderous crash, the poison-drum sounds;
the thieving mind is utterly extinguished, and the eyes grow dazed and bewildered. The hair of the stone maiden stands erect within her dream. Furthermore, the *Luohu Yalu* states:
"The Venerable Master Hongjue Jiyin, at the beginning, attended upon Master Zhenjing at Guizong."
Upon arriving at Feng Peak, one day a guest asked Zhenjing, "How is it with your practice of Chan, Master Hong?
Zhenjing replied, "There are places where you have reached, and there are places where you have not. After the guest had withdrawn, Hong felt uneasy within himself.
He immediately went to Zhenjing to seek resolution for his doubts. Zhenjing recited a verse by Fengxue: "A white cat with sharp claws and talons;
raised in the hall, it leaves no tracks of insects. This is the clear method of establishing oneself upon the tree;

I am merely thinking of going to see him. When the Master of Long’an heard that he was willing to come, he sent someone from Changsha to welcome him, and he resided in the Joyful Hall (Zuile Tang).
On the last day of the sixth month the following year, he asked an attendant about the time of day, and the attendant replied:

"It is already evening," he said with a smile. "We have met within a dream. I have already awakened from my sleep; you need only not betray the monastic community, and that will be repaying the Buddha's kindness.
Having finished speaking, he passed away into stillness.
▲ When Chan Master Lin of the Luoshan Luohan Monastery was about to pass away, he ascended the seat and addressed the assembly, saying:
"Today, the Arhat rides an iron horse backward, ascending Mount Sumeru and trampling through empty space, leaving no trace behind.
He then returned to his quarters, sat in the full lotus posture, and passed away.
▲The Master Huiri of Yongfeng in Xinzhou had attained personal realization under Yunju.

He traveled extensively through the regions of Xiang and Han before returning to Yongfeng, where he lived sometimes in mountain valleys and sometimes in the marketplace. He caused the local people to call him "Master Uncle Qiu.
Whenever anyone questioned him, he would answer with "I do not know. One day, he suddenly said to the townspeople, "I shall go on a pilgrimage tomorrow; you all may..."
They came to see him off, and so those who wished to provide parting gifts gathered in full. The Master laughed incessantly. When the assembly asked him the reason, he immediately wrote a verse:
"Master Qiu, you do not understand; Silent and still, yet bright and clear. At midday, the third watch is struck; Who is able to strike it again?
Having set down his brush, he passed away.
▲The Dharma Master Zunseng Youpeng of Quanzhou once commented upon the *Śūraṃgama-sūtra*, the *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa-sūtra*, and other scriptures; scholars took him as their model.
Yet, he often harbored doubts regarding the path of direct pointing by the Patriarchs, and thus frequently associated with Chan monks. One day, he visited Kaiyuan.
Before his foot had even reached the threshold, [Zhaozhou] suddenly attained realization. Yuanzhu asked, "Master, what have you come for?

The Master replied, "I do not dare to hold my ears in high esteem while disparaging my eyes. Yuanzhu said, "You are quite old; why must you be like this? The Master said, "He who considers himself self-sufficient does not grow.
Yuanzhu said, "I do not question your morning study of the *Avataṃsaka* and your night reading of the *Prajñāpāramitā*; but what is 'the present'?"
Now, a single phrase. The Master said, "The sun is exactly at noon. Yuan said, "Idle words. [The Master] said further, "Speak more!

The Master said, "Throughout my life I have relied on loyalty and trust; today I leave myself to the winds and waves. Although it is thus, what connection is there between this and the Master speaking in such a way?
One must have the new ordinand’s straw sandals worn through. Yuan said, "For now, I let you pass here."

Suddenly meeting Dharma, he asked him, "What would you say? The Master then gave a shout. Yuan said, "This lecturer, today upon seeing the old monk, his spirit charges the Ox and Dipper constellations.
The Master said, "A second offense will not be tolerated. Yuan clapped his hands and laughed loudly.

▲In the summer of the Bingyin year of the Shaoxing era, Chan Master Wujie Jingtan of Yuyang Monastery in Qingyuan Prefecture took leave of the assembly of donors and returned to hand over the affairs of the monastery.
The fourfold assembly crowded around to watch him as he waved his fan for a long time. He then wrote this verse: "This fellow has never had a seam or crack;
Fifty-six years have been spent in idle chatter. Today I die and see King Yama; The Sword-Trees and Blade-Mountains!"
He struck a circle and said, "Aha! Let the various quarters do as they please—drilling tortoises or striking tiles.
He then withdrew his feet and passed away. At his cremation, śarīra relics fell like sleet.
▲ Chan Master Fayan of Wuzu in Qizhou was the son of the Deng family from Mianzhou. At the age of thirty-five, he first left the household life to receive the tonsure and full ordination.
He traveled to Chengdu to study the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra* (The Treatise on Consciousness-Only) and the *Śata-dharmaka-śāstra* (The Treatise on the Hundred Dharmas).

There, he heard that when a Bodhisattva enters the Path of Vision (*darśana-mārga*), wisdom merges with principle and the objective realm unites with the spirit; thus, there is no distinction between the subject that realizes and the object realized. [He then encountered] a non-Buddhist from the Western Regions...
He once challenged a bhikṣu, saying: "Since you do not distinguish between the capacity to realize and that which is realized, by what means then do you realize? No one could answer him.
The non-Buddhists disparaged him, ordering that he be forbidden from sounding the bells and drums and forced to wear the *kāṣāya* robe in reverse.
When the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang arrived there, he resolved this dilemma, saying: "It is like a person drinking cold water; they know its temperature for themselves. The Master then said: "Cold..."
"Warmth" can be understood; however, what is this matter of "self-knowing"? He then went to consult his former lecturer, asking, "I do not know the principle of self-knowing—how does it work?

The lecturer did not dismiss his question, but merely guided him, saying, "If you wish to clarify this, you should go to the South to seek out those who have transmitted the school of the Buddha-mind.
The Master immediately took up his book-bag and crossed the pass. Whichever venerable elders he encountered, there was none who did not...
He consulted [the masters] with these questions, yet his doubts remained unresolved. Eventually, he went to pay his respects to Chan Master Yuanzhao Ben;

at that point, all the karmic conditions of the past and present converged. Only one matter remained unexplained: the story of a monk asking Xinghua, "When they come from the four directions and the eight points, how do you respond?
Xinghua replied, "I strike the one in the center. The monk bowed, and Xinghua said, "Yesterday I attended a village feast, and on the way back, I encountered a sudden..."
In a sudden gale and torrential rain, he sought refuge in an ancient temple. He requested instruction from Yuanben, who said, "This is a karmic encounter from the lineage of Linji;
you must question his descendants before you can understand it. The Master then went to visit Chan Master Fushan Yuan and asked for clarification regarding the previous dialogue.
Yuan said, "I have a parable to tell you: you are just like a three-year-old child..."
A wood-seller in a village was standing at a crossroads with his carrying pole, asking people, "What matters is the Council of State discussing today?
The Master calculated silently, "If this is so, there is still much that remains to be done.
One day, Yuan said to the Master, "I am old; I fear I may let your precious time go to waste. You should go and rely upon Baizhang."

Baizhang said, "Although this old man is of later birth, I have not yet met him in person. However, having seen his verse on the story of Linji’s three blows of the staff, he possesses a quality that transcends ordinary men; he will surely be able to resolve your great matter. The Master wept and took his leave. Upon arriving at Baiyun, he raised the story of the monk asking Nanquan about the *maṇi* jewel for questioning. Baiyun rebuked him, whereupon the Master attained realization and offered a verse of spiritual resonance: A single word, like a thunderbolt, Suddenly shattered my doubt. The entire body is the Buddha, There is no other thing to be found. I have already been enlightened by the Patriarch, Why would I seek it elsewhere? If you wish to see the Buddha, Look directly at your own face. Baiyun approved. He then presented another verse: The Great Way is not difficult, Only avoid picking and choosing. When body and mind are both cast off, The whole universe is one piece. The ten directions are all empty space, Where can the wind and moon go? If you wish to know the Buddha, Look at the face before your parents were born. Baiyun said, "You have truly seen me. He then had the Master serve as his attendant. One day, while they were walking together, Baiyun pointed to a crow and asked, "What is that? The Master replied, "It is a crow. Baiyun said, "What is that crow? The Master was at a loss for words. He said: "A stretch of vacant land before the mountain; with palms joined, I earnestly ask my ancestral father: how many times have you sold it only to buy it back again?
It is out of love for the pines and bamboos that they draw in the pure breeze. Yun granted him approval and ordered him to take charge of the mill.
One day, a monk saw the mill turning and suddenly pointed at it, asking the Master, "Is this supernatural power (ṛddhi) or is it the natural order of things? The Master lifted his robe...
He spun around once, and the monk remained silent. Not long after, Yun arrived and said to the Master, "There are several Zen guests who have come from Mount Lu;
they all possess points of realization. If you ask them to speak, they can speak with justification; if you pose kōans to them, they understand them clearly;
if you ask them to offer a response, they can provide one. Yet, it is simply not yet final. At this, the Master was greatly perplexed.
He thought to himself, "I have already attained awakening; I can explain it and I can clarify it. Why then am I still not 'there'?
He investigated this for several days until, suddenly, he attained realization. All that he had previously cherished was cast aside at once.
He went to see Baiyun, who began to dance with hands and feet; the Master simply smiled. Later, the Master said, "It was because of this that I emerged."
His whole body broke into a cold sweat, and he immediately attained clear realization. One day, Yun said to the assembly: "An ancient said, 'It is like casting an image in a mirror;
once the image is formed, where is the mirror? The assembly offered various responses, but none were in accord. He brought this up to question the Master (Zhaozhou).
The Master stepped forward, paid his respects, and said, 'It is not even close. Yun laughed and said, 'One must be a true practitioner to say such a thing.'"
He then ordered that seats be divided and instructed those yet to come.
The *Xuetang Heshang Shiyilu* states: "When the Fifth Patriarch was at his monastery of ordination, he prostrated himself word by word over the Lotus Sutra."
One night, while encountering the character for "excrement" (shi) and intending to prostrate, he suddenly felt doubt.
He then said to the elder masters, "How can even the character for 'excrement' be called the Dharma-treasure? My prostration has reached this point of uncertainty, which I cannot resolve.
An elder master said, "Based on what you have asked, you may go south to seek instruction; you are truly a vessel of the Zen school. Thereupon, the Patriarch traveled south. At first...
Upon arriving at Xingyuan Prefecture, he remained there for some time. Following the requests of various monasteries, he gradually deviated from his original resolve.
When his preceptor heard of this, he sent a letter to the Patriarch (Linji). The Patriarch opened the seal and saw two lines of writing that said:

"Since you have managed to escape the vinegar vat, you have now become submerged in a soy sauce tub. Having finished reading it, the Patriarch set out on the road that very day, heading toward Zhejiang.
Xīshān first studied under Yuánzhào Běn, and subsequently met Fúshān Yuǎn. Yuǎn marveled at his spiritual capacity and directed him to visit Bái Cūnduān.
Cūnduān instructed him on the causal conditions concerning how the World-Honored One had secret words that Kāśyapa did not conceal. After a long time, he remained without realization.
One day, as he hurried up from the corridor to the Dharma Hall, his doubts were suddenly extinguished. Not long after, Cūnduān appointed him as the head of the grinding mill.
The following is the same as the *Denglu*. Could the matters regarding the *Lijing* recorded in the *Shiyi* refer to events prior to [Baizhang’s] study of *Vijñaptimātratā* in Chengdu?
As for the causal conditions concerning Mahākāśyapa not concealing [the bowl], these are the causal conditions regarding Nanquan’s *maṇi* jewel shown by Baiyun;
as for the matters regarding the Master’s requests for further instruction, the chroniclers each recounted what they had heard. Thus it is that the *Shiyi* contains these records.
Is it perhaps that which was deleted and discarded from the *Gudeng Lu*? The *Shiyi Lu* further states:

One day, in his room, Baiyun raised the case of Yunmen addressing the assembly, "Of such large chestnuts as these, how many can you eat? None of those present offered a response that accorded with the truth.

He questioned his teacher. The teacher said, "To hang up a goat's head while selling dog meat. Yun was startled by this. The teacher once said, "I have studied for twenty years, and only now do I recognize my shame.

Later, when Lingyuan heard of this, he sighed, saying, "Those two words, 'recognizing shame,' are excellent," and thus composed the *Zhengxu Ming* (Inscription on the Continuation of the Lineage), which he subsequently included within the inscription.
There was a layman who sought to leave home under the teacher; he called himself Sheyuan. The teacher—
[The Master] asked, "What is meant by 'conditions for renunciation'? The layman replied, "I have a wife whom I have renounced;
this is called 'conditions for renunciation. The Master said, "I too have a wife. Do you believe me? The layman remained silent. The Master then uttered this verse:
"I have a wife, Whom no one in the world has seen. Day and night we dwell together, Spontaneously possessing skillful means. He recorded this along with [the preceding account].
Bowen asked, "What is the matter under the Linji lineage? The Master said, "The five heinous crimes hearing thunder. He asked, "What is the matter under the Yunmen lineage?
The Master said, "The red banner flickering. He asked, "What is the matter under the Caodong lineage? The Master said, "Dispatching a letter."
He did not go inside. The monk asked, "What is the matter of the Miu-yang lineage? The Master said, "A broken stele lies across the ancient road. The monk bowed.
The Master said, "Why do you not ask about the matter of the Fa-xia lineage? The monk replied, "I shall leave that for the Master. The Master said, "A patrolman violating the curfew.
The monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Bare-chested and barefoot. The monk asked, "What is the Dharma? The Master said:
He did not grant a general amnesty and instead asked, "What is a monk? The Master replied, "Xie Sanlang on the fishing boat.

Jingshan Daoyuan said: "These three turns of phrase each embody the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials, the Four Selections, the Four Hosts and Guests, Dongshan’s Five Ranks, Yunmen’s Three Statements, and hundreds of thousands of Dharma gates with immeasurable subtle meanings. If...

One day, Yuanwu requested instruction, asking, "What are the four guest-host relationships of Linji like? The Master said, "It is merely a matter of following a prescribed course;
what idle business is it? He further said, "In my place, it is like wrestling in front of a horse: you fall down."
He then stopped speaking. The Master said to Yuanwu, "You are quite good, but you have a certain ailment.
Yuanwu asked repeatedly, "I do not know what kind of ailment I have. The Master said, "It is simply that you have too much Zen.

Yuanwu said, "Since it is precisely for the sake of investigating Zen, why do you instead dislike people speaking of Zen? The Master said, "It is because you talk about it too much, as if it were ordinary conversation."

When he was young, he was fond of [the Dharma]. At that time, there was a monk who asked him, "Why do you dislike people speaking of Chan? The Master said, "It is because of my own ill-disposed state of mind.

One day, the Master asked Yuanwu about the "seamless stupa" koan. Yuanwu was at a loss. They walked together from the Abbot’s quarters all the way to the main gate, and only then did Yuanwu manage to speak.
The Master said, "You have spoken it. Yuanwu replied, "Not so. If one is absent for even a moment, one is immediately unfit."
One day, the three Buddhas said to one another, "The Old Monk is merely dry and withered; he often speaks of mind and nature, yet does not grasp them.
Because they requested further instruction, [the Buddha] replied, "The Buddha-body is unconditioned and does not fall into numerical categories.
The Master said, "It is like a pure maṇi jewel reflecting the five colors: the five colors are the numbers, while the maṇi is the Buddha-body, perfectly round."
Wu said to the two elders, "He understands and speaks with great depth. When we speak, we expend so much effort, yet he finishes with only one or two sentences.
He is clearly a great beast. Upon hearing this, the Master said, "If one speaks of mind or nature, that is indeed foul speech.
He further remarked, "The cat has the merit of drinking blood; the tiger has the power to raise the dead."

The Master was about to answer, but Letan struck him and shouted, "What do you call this 'Chan'? The Master suddenly grasped the essential meaning and immediately said, "Chan has no after."

There is nothing prior. The waves are clear in the great ocean; the moon is reflected in the blue sky. Again he asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "The Way is amidst the vast expanse of red dust;
there is no need for contrivance. It is fundamentally without lack or deficiency. [He remained] profoundly still.
Huanji said: "Pitiful! For ten thousand kalpas, one is tethered to the hitching post for donkeys.
Having resided at Zhongfeng and Qiyun in the midst of Xuedou for more than twenty years, a monk arrived to pay his respects. The Master said:

"Where did you come from recently? he asked. "From Tiantong," the monk replied. The Master said, "How high is Mount Taibai? The monk struck his forehead with his hand and made a gesture of looking up.
The Master said, "There is still this one remaining. "Then please let the abbot of the hermitage say it," the monk requested. The Master then made the same gesture of striking his forehead.
As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him. He lived at Lingshu for thirty years; during that time, he dwelt in solitude without possessing anything beyond his basic necessities.
Two tigers attended to his right side. One day, they became so fierce toward people that he dismissed them with a verse.

On the twelfth day of the fourth month in the seventh year of the Xuanhua era, he passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture. The Official Censor Chen composed a detailed account of the Master’s life and deeds, including the extraordinary signs that appeared during his illness;
furthermore, he had a statue of him fashioned with the two tigers attending him, which remains to this day.

▲ Chan Master Cishi Ruixian of Shaoxing Prefecture practiced the *vinaya*. Upon observing that the nature of the precepts is like empty space and that those who cling to them are deluded, the Master said:

Through the ten objects and ten vehicles, consciousness is transformed into wisdom. Only through the contemplation of the inconceivable realm does wisdom shine forth."
[The Master] Ming [Zhiyan] realized that this was beyond the reach of verbal expression. He traveled to visit various masters in different regions and eventually arrived at Touzi.

Guangjian asked, "Where is your native place? The Master replied, "Dongyue in the two provinces of Zhejiang. Guangjian asked, "What is the situation in Dongyue? The Master said, "The Qinwang Peak is high; the Lake of Tonghu is broad.

▲ Prime Minister Zhang Shangying was a lay practitioner whose courtesy name was Tianjue and whose style was Wujin.

At the age of nineteen, he traveled to the capital to take the imperial examinations. On his way, he passed by the residence of the Xiang family. One evening prior to his arrival, a deity had appeared in a dream to the head of the household, saying, "I shall welcome the Prime Minister.

When the official arrived, the Xiang family agreed to give him their daughter in marriage. After he had passed the examinations, he married the lady of the Xiang family. One day, the official saw that the binding and decoration of the Tripitaka scriptures were magnificent.

Lì was displeased and said, "Among the things people revere and serve, the sages' writings do not even mention this. I wish to compose a 'Treatise on the Non-existence of the Buddha. Xiang said, "If there is no Buddha, what is there to discuss?
You must first compose a 'Treatise on the Existence of the Buddha' before you can proceed. Gōng doubted these words and consequently desisted.
Later, he visited his colleagues and saw that they had just finished reading the *Vimalakīrti Sūtra*, at which point it reached the passage: "Sickness is not the element of earth..."
Nor was it separate from the element of earth. He marveled, saying, "Can the speech of these barbarians be so eloquent? He then borrowed the work to read through it.

When Lady Xiang asked what book he was reading, the Master said, "The Vimalakīrti Sūtra. Lady Xiang said, "You should read this thoroughly before composing your 'Treatise on the Non-existence of the Buddha.
The Master was struck with awe and consequently gained deep faith in the Buddha Vehicle. In the sixth year of the Yuanyou era, he served as the Fiscal Commissioner of Jiangxi.
He first visited Donglin Zong, who interrogated him regarding his insights; finding them to coincide with his own, Zong granted him formal approval (*inka*).
He was then instructed to go see Zong’s disciple, Yuxi Cigujing. While Gong was governing Ningbo, various Chan practitioners came to welcome him.
Gong paid his respects to Ci and, having heard that Gong Dezhuang once remarked that Doushui Yue was exceptionally intelligent, he asked Yue: "I have heard that you are skilled in..."
Wen Zhang said with a smile, "As for me, Congyue am the ninth-generation descendant of Linji. For me to discuss literature with you, Commissioner, is exactly like your discussing Chan with me.
The official did not agree with his words. The official insisted on counting on his fingers and said, "That makes nine generations.
He asked, "How far is Yuxi from here? Wen Zhang replied, "Thirty li. He asked, "How far is Doushuai? Wen Zhang replied, "Five li. Thereupon—
He passed through the Tuṣita Heaven. Previously, while dreaming, he had grasped the sun’s disk with his hand. Upon waking, he said to the head seat:

"The image of the sun’s movement signifies that Commissioner Zhang will soon pass by here; I shall deeply pierce and sharply prick him. The head seat said, "Scholars and officials detest those who oppose them;
they may perhaps give rise to further trouble. Yuè said, "Even if it causes affliction, it will only serve to cause him to withdraw from my monastery."
While Master Gong was conversing with Yue, he praised Donglin. Yue was unwilling to accept his assessment, so Gong composed a poem for Baoxuan, which included the lines:
"If one does not seek the place of descent on Mount Lu, the elephant-king’s nostrils will idly poke at the sky. The meaning was a critique of Yue’s refusal to acknowledge Donglin.
As Gong and Yue spoke until late into the night, their discussion turned to the affairs of the Chan school, whereupon Yue said:

Donglin having already granted his seal of approval to the Commissioner, [the Master] asked, "Does the Commissioner have even the slightest doubt regarding the words and teachings of the Buddhas and patriarchs?
The official replied, "I do. Yue asked, "What words do you doubt? The official said, "I doubt the 'One-legged Verse' of Xiangyan and the story of Deshan’s alms-bowl."

Yue said, "Since you have doubts regarding this, how can you possibly be without them regarding the rest? Take, for instance, Yantou’s words concerning 'the final phrase'—does it exist or does it not?
Gong replied, "It exists. Yue laughed loudly and returned to his quarters, closing the door behind him.

The Master did not sleep soundly throughout the night. At the fifth watch, he descended from his bed and accidentally overturned his urinal. Thereupon, he attained great enlightenment and suddenly realized the meaning of the previous dialogue.
He then composed a verse, which says: "The drum falls silent and the bell is hushed as the bowl is carried back; Yantou’s single thrust was like a clap of thunder."
"Indeed, you shall live for only three years. "Was it not because you received a prophecy from him?

Yuanze said, "Commissioner, please depart; let us meet tomorrow. The next day, the official recited the previous verse. Yuanze then said to him, "The purpose of practicing Zen is simply this..."
The life-faculty remains unbroken; understanding arises based on speech. You, Gong, have already deeply realized such a teaching.

Yet, when it comes to the most subtle point, it causes people not to perceive or know it, and they fall into the realm of dualistic existence. Thus, he composed a verse to testify to this: "In the midst of ordinary activity, every step is as it should be.

There is no distinction. Cease differentiating between essence and function; do not select between the refined and the coarse. Unimpeded when confronting the opportune moment, free from constraints when responding to phenomena.
When the sentiments of right and wrong are exhausted, both ordinary and sage are eliminated. Who gains and who loses? What is near and what is distant?

To take the head as the tail, to point at reality as being empty—to turn one's body in the realm of Māra and shift one's feet onto the path of the heterodox—therein is neither opposition nor conformity, and no effort is ever violated. You have invited me, sir.
Yue arrived at Jianchang. Along the way, he observed everything one by one, composing ten verses to describe these matters; Yue also composed ten verses in response.

The Master once said: "What the Buddhas of the past have taught—that within the tip of a single hair there appears a jeweled king-land, and that while sitting within a mote of dust one turns the Great Wheel of Dharma—is the true meaning.

This matter is not merely a formal expression of the Dharma. On the dawn of the eleventh month in the fourth year of the Xuanhua era, he dictated his final testament with his own mouth and commanded his disciples to write it down.
Suddenly, he took up his pillow and threw it against the door and window; the sound was like a peal of thunder.

▲ Chan Master Xian Zhengjue of the Xinsiang School in Chengdu Prefecture was renowned as a young man for his success in the jinshi examinations.

Once, while playing by scooping up mountain stream water during the day, he thought of it at night; subsequently, he saw the water fill the room with a shimmering clarity. He wished to draw some up, but it could not be taken, and the mundane world naturally vanished before him.
He exclaimed, "The net of worldly existence has been torn asunder! He went to rely upon Master Zhaojue to receive ordination and fully realized the precepts.

He divided the precepts. Later, he followed the assembly to seek instruction. One day, Yuanjue asked the Master, "Standing atop the high peak, walking upon the deep ocean floor—how do you understand this?
At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment and said, "My heels have been nailed down.
Yuanjue raised his whisk and asked, "What about this one? The Master smiled and departed. He served [Yuanjue] diligently for seven years.
He traveled south to the capital and passed through Huai and Zhe. Later, he met Master Wuzu Yan at Haihui Temple.
Stepping forward, he asked: "I do not yet know the pivot; it is difficult to cross Zhaozhou’s bridge. "I shall not ask about Zhaozhou’s bridge," he continued, "but what is the pivot?
The Master said, "Stay outside the gate for now. The student stepped forward, gave a kick, and withdrew. The Master said, "I grant you."

After a long time over tea and rice, it turns out there was someone who truly knew the flavor. The next day, when the Master entered the room, the Patriarch said, "Are you the monk who questioned me yesterday?
I certainly know where your understanding lies; it is simply that you have not yet passed the Baiyun Barrier.
The Master said, "I take my leave," and departed. At that time, Yuanwu was serving as the attendant. The Master [later] explained the meaning of the Baiyun Barrier to him.
He tapped him. Wuzhuo said, "You simply need to realize it directly. The Master laughed and said, "It is not that I do not understand; it is simply that I am not yet familiar with it.

The Master said, "I am here to attend to you. The Patriarch looked at Wuzhuo and said, "This fellow talks too much. From that time on, their karmic conditions were in accord.
Upon returning from his travels to Mount Lu, the Master told the Fifth Patriarch the words he had received while standing atop the highest peak and walking upon the bottom of the deepest sea.
